pairs.he: וְעַל כֵּן קִבְּצָם וְצִוָּם וּבֵרְכָם, כִּי כָּל הַבְּרָכוֹת הֵם בְּחִינַת הַמְשָׁכַת הַדַּעַת הַנַּ״ל לְהוֹדִיעָם הָאֱמוּנָה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה שֶׁזֶּה עִקַּר כְּלַל הַבְּרָכוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם, בְּחִינַת אֲשֶׁר הַמִּתְבָּרֵךְ בָּאָרֶץ יִתְבָּרֵךְ בֵּאלֹקֵי אָמֵן. כִּי כָּל הַטּוֹבוֹת וְהַבְּרָכוֹת וְכָל הַהַשְׁפָּעוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם בְּגַשְׁמִיּוּת וְרוּחָנִיּוּת כֻּלָּם נִמְשָׁכִין מֵהַדַּעַת הַנַּ״ל, בְּחִינַת דַּעַת קָנִיתָ מֶה חָסַרְתָּ, כִּי תַּכְלִית הַדַּעַת הַנַּ״ל לֵידַע וּלְהַכִּיר אֶת הַבּוֹרֵא יִתְבָּרַךְ, הוּא הַבְּרָכָה. דְּהַיְנוּ לְהוֹדוֹת וּלְהַלֵּל וּלְבָרֵךְ אוֹתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּכָל עֵת עַל כָּל דָּבָר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁתִּקְּנוּ לָנוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּרָכוֹת עַל כָּל הַדְּבָרִים שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם, שֶׁכָּל אֵלּוּ הַבְּרָכוֹת הֵם בְּחִינַת הַמְשָׁכַת הַדַּעַת הַנַּ״ל, שֶׁאָנוּ צְרִיכִין לְהוֹדִיעַ לְכָל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם בְּכָל פַּעַם כִּי ה׳ הוּא הָאֱלֹקִים וְהוּא בָּרָא וְיָצַר וְעָשָׂה הַכֹּל וּמְקַיֵּם הַכֹּל וּמַנְהִיג וּמַשְׁגִּיחַ בְּכָל עֵת, וְהוּא בְּרַחֲמָיו מַזְמִין וּמַשְׁפִּיעַ לָנוּ כָּל דָּבָר וְדָבָר בַּחֲסְדּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
pairs.en: And therefore he gathered them, instructed them, and blessed them; for all the blessings are the aspect of drawing forth the aforementioned understanding, to make known to them the holy faith, which is the principal entirety of the blessings in the world, the aspect of “He who blesses himself in the land shall bless himself by the God of Amen.” For all the good things and blessings and all the influences in the world, materially and spiritually, are all drawn from the aforementioned understanding, the aspect of “You have acquired understanding—what do you lack?” For the purpose of the aforementioned understanding—to know and recognize the blessed Creator—is the blessing. That is, to thank, praise, and bless Him, blessed be He, at every time for every matter, as our sages of blessed memory instituted for us blessings over all the things in the world. All these blessings are the aspect of drawing forth the aforementioned understanding: we must make known to all who enter the world on every occasion that the Lord is God, and He created, formed, and made everything, sustains everything, and leads and watches over everything at every time; and He, in His mercy, provides and bestows upon us each and every thing in the particulars of particulars.

qualifiedAfter.en: And therefore he gathered them, instructed them, and blessed them; for all the blessings are the aspect of drawing forth the aforementioned understanding, to make known to them the holy faith, which is the principal entirety of the blessings in the world, the aspect of “He who blesses himself in the land shall bless himself by the God of Amen.” For all the good things and blessings and all the influences in the world, materially and spiritually, are all drawn from the aforementioned understanding, the aspect of “You have acquired understanding—what do you lack?” For the purpose of the aforementioned understanding—to know and recognize the blessed Creator—is the blessing. That is, to thank, praise, and bless Him, blessed be He, at every time for every matter, as our sages of blessed memory instituted for us blessings over all the things in the world. All these blessings are the aspect of drawing forth the aforementioned understanding: we must make known to all who enter the world on every occasion that the Lord is God, and He created, formed, and made everything, sustains everything, and leads and watches over everything at every time; and He, in His mercy, provides and bestows upon us each and every thing in the particulars of particulars.

pairs.he: וְעַל יְדֵי הַבְּרָכוֹת שֶׁאָנוּ מְבָרְכִין אוֹתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל יְדֵי זֶה מַמְשִׁיכִין עָלֵינוּ כָּל הַבְּרָכוֹת וְכָל הַהַשְׁפָּעוֹת טוֹבוֹת, כִּי הַמְבָרֵךְ מִתְבָּרֵךְ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה. בְּחִינַת טוֹב עַיִן הוּא יְבֹרַךְ, ׳יְבָרֵךְ׳, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה.
pairs.en: Through the blessings with which we bless Him, blessed be He, through this we draw upon ourselves all the blessings and all the good influences, for the one who blesses is blessed, as our sages of blessed memory said. The aspect of “One of good eye shall be blessed”—“shall bless,” as our sages of blessed memory said.

qualifiedAfter.en: Through the blessings with which we bless Him, blessed be He, through this we draw upon ourselves all the blessings and all the good influences, for the one who blesses is blessed, as our sages of blessed memory said. The aspect of “One of good eye shall be blessed”—“shall bless,” as our sages of blessed memory said.

pairs.he: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת כָּל הַבְּרָכוֹת שֶׁבֵּרַךְ יַעֲקֹב וּמֹשֶׁה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל קֹדֶם הִסְתַּלְּקוּתָם, שֶׁכֻּלָּם הָיוּ בְּחִינַת הַמְשָׁכַת הַדַּעַת הַקָּדוֹשׁ הַנַּ״ל. וְעַל כֵּן כְּלָלִיּוּת בִּרְכוֹתֵיהֶם אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה שֶׁיִּתְגַּבְּרוּ לִכְבֹּשׁ אֶת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וּלְהַכְנִיעַ וּלְשַׁבֵּר הַשּׂוֹנְאִים הַפּוֹגְעִים מִקְּדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל כַּמּוּבָן בְּפֵרוּשׁ רַשִׁ״י וּבְכָל דִּבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה.
pairs.en: This is the aspect of all the blessings with which Yaakov and Moshe blessed Israel before their departure, all of which were the aspect of drawing forth the aforementioned holy understanding. Therefore the generality of their blessings of Israel was that they should strengthen themselves to conquer the land of Israel and to subdue and break the enemies who strike against the holiness of Israel, as is understood in Rashi’s commentary and in all the words of our sages of blessed memory.

pairs.he: שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּחִינַת מַה שֶׁבֵּרַךְ אֶת יְהוּדָה, ״גּוּר אַרְיֵה יְהוּדָה״. שֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנּוּ דָּוִד שֶׁלָּחַם מִלְחֲמוֹת ה׳ לְהַכְנִיעַ הָעַכּוּ״ם שֶׁהֵם כְּנֶגֶד אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל. וְכֵן ״גָּד גְּדוּד יְגוּדֶנּוּ וְכוּ׳״. וְכֵן כֻּלָּם וְכֵן בִּרְכָתוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה שֶׁהָיָה מֵעֵין בִּרְכָתוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה. כִּי עִקַּר הַדַּעַת הַנַּ״ל נִמְשָׁךְ רַק בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁשָּׁם הַבַּיִת הַמִּקְדָּשׁ שֶׁשָּׁם עִקַּר הַדַּעַת שֶׁל בְּחִינַת בֵּן וְתַלְמִיד.
pairs.en: This is the aspect of his blessing Yehudah: “Yehudah is a lion cub”—for David issued from him and fought the wars of the Lord to subdue the Akum, who oppose the land of Israel. Likewise, “Gad—a troop shall troop against him,” etc.; and likewise all of them. And likewise Moshe’s blessing, which was of the nature of Yaakov’s blessing, as our sages of blessed memory said. For the principal aforementioned understanding is drawn forth only in the land of Israel, where the Temple is, where the principal understanding of the aspect of son and disciple is.

segments.he:
יעקב אמר להם שהעצה הוא שיהיה ביניהם אחדות ושלום

״הֵאָסְפוּ וְאַגִּידָה לָכֶם״

(מ״ט, א)

זֶה ״וַיִּקְרָא יַעֲקֹב לְבָנָיו וַיֹּאמֶר הֵאָסְפוּ וְאַגִּידָה לָכֶם אֵת אֲשֶׁר יִקְרָא אֶתְכֶם בְּאַחֲרִית הַיָּמִים״. שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ לְגַלּוֹת אֶת הַקֵּץ וְכוּ׳, כִּי עִקַּר הַקֵּץ תָּלוּי בָּעֵצָה שְׁלֵמָה הַנַּ״ל שֶׁמִּתְגַּלֶּה עַל יְדֵי מָשִׁיחַ שֶׁנִּקְרָא פֶּלֶא יוֹעֵץ, כִּי עִקַּר קֵץ הַגְּאֻלָּה תָּלוּי בְּעֵצוֹת עֲמֻקּוֹת שֶׁהֵם עֲמֻקִּים מְאֹד מְאֹד שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲמֹד עֲלֵיהֶם שׁוּם נָבִיא וְחוֹזֶה, שֶׁעֲלֵיהֶם נֶאֱמַר כִּי ה׳ צְבָאוֹת יָעָץ וּמִי יָפֵר וְכוּ׳. וְעַל כֵּן הוּא קֵץ הַפְּלָאוֹת, וְעַל כֵּן אֲפִלּוּ יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ כְּשֶׁרָצָה לְגַלּוֹת הַקֵּץ, הַיְנוּ שֶׁרָצָה לְגַלּוֹת הָעֵצוֹת הָעֲמֻקּוֹת מְאֹד שֶׁעַל יָדָם יָבֹא הַקֵּץ, אֲזַי נִסְתַּלֵּק הֵימֶנּוּ שְׁכִינָה, כִּי אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְגַלּוֹתָם בִּפְרָט אָז שֶׁהָיָה עֲדַיִן קֹדֶם הַתְחָלַת הַגָּלוּת הָרִאשׁוֹן וְקֹדֶם קַבָּלַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁמִּשָּׁם עִקַּר הַמְשָׁכַת הָעֵצוֹת עֲמֻקּוֹת כַּנַּ״ל.

וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר הִקָּבְצוּ וְשִׁמְעוּ בְּנֵי יַעֲקֹב, ׳הִקָּבְצוּ׳ דַּיְקָא, שֶׁגִּלָּה לָהֶם שֶׁעִקַּר יְסוֹד תִּקּוּן הָעֵצָה הוּא בְּחִינַת ׳הִקָּבְצוּ׳, הַיְנוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אַחְדוּת וְאַהֲבָה וְשָׁלוֹם בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁיִּתְקַבְּצוּ יַחַד לְדַבֵּר זֶה עִם זֶה מֵהַתַּכְלִית הָאַחֲרוֹן, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִזְכּוּ לִשְׁלֵמוּת הָעֵצָה, כִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאוֹרַיְתָא כֻּלָּא חַד, כִּי הַשָּׁלוֹם וְהָאַחְדוּת שֶׁבֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּמוֹ כֵן נִתְאַחֵד הָעֵצָה יַחַד שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּקְרֵאת עֵצָה כַּנַּ״ל. כִּי י״ב בְּנֵי יַעֲקֹב שֶׁהֵם כְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, הֵם בְּחִינַת י״ב בְּנֵי יַעֲקֹב שֶׁנִּכְלְלוּ יַחַד בָּאֶבֶן שְׁתִיָּה, שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּחִינַת שְׁלֵמוּת הָעֵצָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּבֹאָר שָׁם בְּהַתּוֹרָה הַנַּ״ל). שֶׁכָּל זֶה תָּלוּי בְּאַהֲבָה וְשָׁלוֹם, בְּחִינַת אָזֶן בַּחֲבִירוּתָא תַּלְיָא. (כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּבֹאָר שָׁם, עַיֵּן שָׁם).

(הלכות תשעה באב ותעניות הלכה ד׳ אות י״ג)
segments.en:
Yaakov told them that the counsel is that there should be unity and peace among them.

“Gather together, and I shall tell you.”

(49:1)

This is “And Yaakov called to his sons and said: Gather together, and I shall tell you what will happen to you at the end of days.” He wished to reveal the end, etc., for the principal end depends upon the aforementioned complete counsel that is revealed through Messiah, who is called Wondrous Counselor. For the principal end of redemption depends upon deep counsels that are exceedingly, exceedingly deep, which no prophet or seer can comprehend. Concerning them it is said, “For the Lord of Hosts has counseled, and who shall annul it,” etc. And therefore it is the end of wonders. And therefore even Yaakov our father, when he wished to reveal the end—that is, when he wished to reveal the exceedingly deep counsels through which the end will come—the Divine Presence then departed from him. For they cannot be revealed, especially then, when it was still before the beginning of the first exile and before the receiving of Torah, from which the principal drawing forth of deep counsels proceeds, as stated above.

And therefore he said, “Gather together and listen, sons of Yaakov”—specifically “Gather together”—revealing to them that the principal foundation of the rectification of counsel is the aspect of “Gather together”: that there should be unity, love, and peace among Israel, that they gather together to speak with one another about the final purpose. And through this they will merit completeness of counsel, for Israel and Torah are all one. For in accordance with the peace and unity among Israel, counsel likewise becomes united together, which is the aspect of Torah, called counsel, as stated above. For the twelve sons of Yaakov, who are the entirety of Israel, are the aspect of the twelve sons of Yaakov who were included together in the foundation stone, which is the aspect of completeness of counsel (as explained there in the aforementioned discourse). All this depends upon love and peace, the aspect of “The ear depends upon companionship”. (As explained there; see there.)

(Laws of Tishuh Bi’Av and Taaniyos, law 4, item 13)

יעקב ראה שאי אפשר לדחוק את הקץ

״הֵאָסְפוּ וְאַגִּידָה לָכֶם אֵת אֲשֶׁר יִקְרָה אֶתְכֶם בְּאַחֲרִית הַיָּמִים״

(מ״ט, א)

וְאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ בִּקֵּשׁ לְגַלּוֹת אֶת הַקֵּץ וְנִסְתַּלְּקָה הֵימֶנּוּ שְׁכִינָה, אָמַר, שֶׁמָּא יֵשׁ בֵּינֵיכֶם פָּסוּל כְּשֵׁם וְכוּ׳. מִיָּד פָּתְחוּ כֻּלָּם וְאָמְרוּ, שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל ה׳ אֱלֹקֵינוּ ה׳ אֶחָד, כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין בְּלִבְּךָ אֶלָּא אֶחָד כָּךְ אֵין בְּלִבֵּנוּ אֶלָּא אֶחָד. וְאָז הִתְחִיל לְדַבֵּר דְּבָרִים אֲחֵרִים וְקִנְטֵר אֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים רְאוּבֵן וְשִׁמְעוֹן וְכוּ׳. הַיְנוּ כִּי יַעֲקֹב עֵת שֶׁבַּתְּחִלָּה סָבַר שֶׁכְּבָר הִגִּיעַ הָעֵת לְגַלּוֹת לָהֶם אֶת הַקֵּץ וְנִסְתַּלְּקָה הֵימֶנּוּ שְׁכִינָה וְעַל כֵּן סָבַר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם אֵיזֶה פָּסוּל כַּנַּ״ל. כֵּיוָן שֶׁאָמְרוּ שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּ׳ וְרָאָה שֶׁכָּל הָעֵדָה כֻּלָּם קְדוֹשִׁים וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן נִסְתַּלְּקָה מִמֶּנּוּ שְׁכִינָה עַל שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ לְגַלּוֹת אֶת הַקֵּץ, שֶׁאָז הֵבִין מִיָּד שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִדְחֹק אֶת הַשָּׁעָה בְּשׁוּם דָּבָר, וּבִפְרָט בְּעִנְיַן הַקֵּץ הָאַחֲרוֹן לָשׁוּב לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְשֶׁתִּהְיֶה גְּאֻלָּה שְׁלֵמָה שֶׁאֵין אַחֲרֶיהָ גָּלוּת, שֶׁזֶּה נֶעְלָם מִכָּל הַצַּדִּיקִים הַגְּדוֹלִים וַאֲפִלּוּ הַצַּדִּיקִים הַיּוֹדְעִים בָּזֶה קְצָת אָסוּר לְגַלּוֹת כִּי לִבָּה לְפוּמָה לֹא גָּלֵי, וְאָז הֵבִין גֹּדֶל הַפְּגָם שֶׁל הַדּוֹחֵק אֶת הַשָּׁעָה אֲפִלּוּ צַדִּיקִים גְּדוֹלִים.

וזה מה שהוכיח את ג׳ השבטים שזה היה הפגם שלהם בחינה זו של דוחק את השעה

וְעַל כֵּן אָז הִתְחִיל לְקַנְטֵר אֶת הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה שְׁבָטִים עַל פְּגָמֵיהֶם, וְעִקַּר הַפְּגָם שֶׁלָּהֶם הָיָה בְּעִנְיַן הַדּוֹחֵק אֶת הַשָּׁעָה. בְּחִינַת פַּחַז כַּמַּיִם אַל תּוֹתַר הַיְנוּ שֶׁבָּלְבַל בְּחִפָּזוֹן וּבֶהָלָה גְּדוֹלָה וּבִלְבֵּל יְצוּעֵי אָבִיו, וְעִקַּר הַפְּגָם הָיָה בִּבְחִינַת דּוֹחֵק אֶת הַשָּׁעָה בְּחִינַת פַּחַז כַּמַּיִם, כִּי רְאוּבֵן הָיָה בְּוַדַּאי צַדִּיק גָּדוֹל וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה, כָּל הָאוֹמֵר רְאוּבֵן חָטָא אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא טוֹעֶה. רַק שֶׁהַפְּגָם שֶׁלּוֹ הָיָה שֶׁקִּנֵּא קִנְאַת אִמּוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה וּבֶאֱמֶת גַּם זֶה הָיָה פְּגָם גָּדוֹל וְעִקַּר הַפְּגָם בִּבְחִינַת הַדּוֹחֵק אֶת הַשָּׁעָה.

וּבָזֶה פּוֹגְמִים גַּם עַתָּה צַדִּיקִים וּכְשֵׁרִים וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי וְהֵבַנְתִּי מִפִּיו הַקָּדוֹשׁ זִכְרוֹ צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה שֶׁאָמַר, שֶׁזֶּה יֵצֶר הָרַע גָּדוֹל אֵצֶל כַּמָּה בְּנֵי אָדָם, וּבִפְרָט הַגְּדוֹלִים בְּמַעֲלָה שֶׁבִּשְׁבִיל דָּבָר אֶחָד שֶׁנִּדְמֶה לָהֶם שֶׁהוּא מִצְוָה הֵם מַפְקִירִים הַכֹּל וּבָאִים עַל יְדֵי זֶה לִידֵי קִלְקוּלִים רַבִּים וּבִפְרָט כְּשֶׁבָּאִים עַל יְדֵי זֶה לִידֵי מַחֲלֹקֶת. וּכְשֶׁנְּעַיֵּן בְּכָל הַמַּעֲשִׂיּוֹת שֶׁהָיָה בֵּין הַצַּדִּיקִים בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר הַכֹּל הָיָה בִּבְחִינָה זֹאת, שֶׁהַבַּעַל דָּבָר הִטְעָה אוֹתָם כְּאִלּוּ שֶׁכְּנֶגְדּוֹ פּוֹגֵם הַרְבֵּה וּמִצְוָה לִמְסֹר נֶפֶשׁ לְרָדְפוֹ וְכוּ׳.

וּבֶאֱמֶת שָׁגוּ בָּזֶה מְאֹד, כִּי עַל יְדֵי הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת וְהַכַּעַס אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְתַקֵּן בְּשׁוּם אֹפֶן רַק צְרִיכִין לְהִתְיַשֵּׁב הַרְבֵּה אֵיךְ לְהִתְנַהֵג בָּזֶה. וְהָעִקָּר לְבַקֵּשׁ מֵה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיַּנְחֵהוּ בְּדֶרֶךְ הָאֱמֶת וּלְהִתְיַשֵּׁב עַצְמוֹ הַרְבֵּה אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ כֹּחַ לְרָדְפוֹ, וְאוּלַי כַּוָּנָתוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁנִי לְשָׁמַיִם רַק שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהָבִין דְּבָרָיו. וְגַם אָמְרוּ עָלָיו הַרְבֵּה שְׁקָרִים וּכְזָבִים, בְּחִינַת אֲשֶׁר לֹא גָזַלְתִּי אָז אָשִׁיב. וְיֵשׁ בָּזֶה הַרְבֵּה לְדַבֵּר.

וְזֶה הָיָה בְּחִינַת הַפְּגָם שֶׁל רְאוּבֵן, שֶׁכַּוָּנָתוֹ בְּוַדַּאי לְשָׁמַיִם כִּי קִנֵּא קִנְאַת אִמּוֹ. אַף עַל פִּי כֵן פָּגַם בָּזֶה מְאֹד עַד שֶׁאָבַד עַל יְדֵי זֶה הַכְּהֻנָּה וְהַמַּלְכוּת וְכָל הַפְּגָם הָיָה בִּבְחִינַת דּוֹחֵק אֶת הַשָּׁעָה בְּחִינַת פַּחַז כַּמַּיִם אַל תּוֹתַר וְכוּ׳ כַּנַּ״ל:

וּבִפְרָט שִׁמְעוֹן וְלֵוִי שָׁגוּ בָּזֶה הַרְבֵּה יוֹתֵר, כִּי מָכְרוּ אֶת יוֹסֵף שֶׁהַכֹּל הָיָה בִּבְחִינָה הַנַּ״ל שֶׁדָּחֲקוּ אֶת הַשָּׁעָה. וְסָבְרוּ שֶׁיְּתַקְּנוּ הָעוֹלָם עַל יְדֵי מְכִירַת יוֹסֵף, כִּי רָאוּ שֶׁמֵּבִיא אֶת דִּבָּתָם רָעָה אֶל אֲבִיהֶם וְרָאוּ שֶׁיָּצְאוּ מִמֶּנּוּ יָרָבְעָם וְאַחְאָב. עַל כֵּן לְפִי דַּעְתָּם רָצוּ לְהָרְגוֹ וְכַוָּנָתָם הָיָה בִּשְׁבִיל תִּקּוּן הָעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא יֵצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ יָרָבְעָם וְאַחְאָב וְכֵן שְׁאָרֵי סְבָרוֹת שֶׁל טָעוּת שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם בָּזֶה. כִּי בְּוַדַּאי הָיוּ צַדִּיקִים גְּדוֹלִים אַךְ שָׁגוּ הַרְבֵּה וְעִקַּר הַפְּגָם הָיָה בִּבְחִינַת דּוֹחֵק הַשָּׁעָה כַּנַּ״ל. וְזֶה שֶׁקִּנְטְרָם שִׁמְעוֹן וְלֵוִי אַחִים כְּלֵי חָמָס מְכֵרוֹתֵיהֶם. כְּלֵי חָמָס דַּיְקָא בְּחִינַת חָמָס וְגֶזֶל שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה הַפְּגָם שֶׁלָּהֶם, כִּי הַדּוֹחֵק אֶת הַשָּׁעָה אֲפִלּוּ אִם הוּא צַדִּיק הוּא בְּחִינַת גַּזְלָן וְחַמְסָן כַּנַּ״ל.

(הלכות גזילה הלכה ה׳ אות י׳)
segments.en:
Yaakov saw that it is impossible to force the end.

“Gather together, and I shall tell you what will happen to you at the end of days.”

(49:1)

And our sages of blessed memory said that Yaakov our father wished to reveal the end, and the Divine Presence departed from him. He said: Perhaps there is an unfit one among you, just as, etc. Immediately they all began and said: “Hear, Israel: the Lord is our God; the Lord is one. Just as in your heart there is only one, so in our heart there is only one.” And then he began speaking of other matters and reproved the tribes, Reuven and Shimon, etc. That is, initially Yaakov thought that the time had already come to reveal the end to them, and the Divine Presence departed from him; and therefore he thought that there was some unfitness among them, as stated above. Once they said “Hear, Israel,” etc., and he saw that the whole congregation was entirely holy, yet nevertheless the Divine Presence had departed from him because he wished to reveal the end, then he immediately understood that it is impossible to force the hour in any matter. And especially concerning the final end—returning to the land of Israel and there being a complete redemption after which there is no exile—this is concealed from all the great righteous ones. And even the righteous who know a little about it are forbidden to reveal it, for the heart does not disclose it to the mouth. And then he understood the magnitude of the blemish of one who forces the hour—even great righteous ones.

And this is what he reproved the three tribes for: this was their blemish, this aspect of forcing the hour.

Therefore he then began to reprove the three tribes concerning their blemishes, and the principal blemish they had was in the matter of forcing the hour. The aspect of “Hasty as water, you shall not have preeminence”: that is, he acted disruptively in haste and great agitation and disturbed his father’s couches; and the principal blemish was in the aspect of forcing the hour, the aspect of “Hasty as water.” For Reuven was certainly a great righteous man, and as our sages of blessed memory said: Anyone who says Reuven sinned is only mistaken. Rather, his blemish was that he was zealous for his mother’s cause, as our sages of blessed memory said. In truth, this too was a great blemish, and the principal blemish was in the aspect of forcing the hour.

And in this, even now righteous and upright people cause a blemish. And this is as I heard and understood from his holy mouth—may the memory of the righteous be for a blessing—when he said that this is a great evil inclination among several people, especially those of high standing: for the sake of one thing that seems to them to be a commandment, they abandon everything, and through this come to many corruptions, especially when through this they come into controversy. And when we examine all the episodes that occurred among the righteous in every generation, everything was in this aspect: the Baal Davar misled them, as though the person opposing him blemishes greatly and it were a commandment to give one’s life to pursue him, etc.

And in truth they erred greatly in this, for through controversy and anger it is impossible to rectify in any manner. Rather, one must deliberate greatly about how to conduct oneself in this. And the principal thing is to ask the blessed Lord to lead him in the way of truth, and to deliberate greatly whether he has the strength to pursue him. And perhaps the other person’s intention is for Heaven, but his words cannot be understood; and they also said many lies and falsehoods about him—the aspect of “What I did not steal, then I shall restore.” And there is much to say about this.

This was the aspect of Reuven’s blemish: his intention was certainly for Heaven, for he was zealous for his mother’s cause. Nevertheless, he blemished this greatly, until through this he lost the priesthood and the kingship. The entire blemish was in the aspect of forcing the hour, the aspect of “Hasty as water, you shall not have preeminence,” etc., as stated above:

Shimon and Levi in particular erred in this much more, for they sold Yosef, and all this was in the aforementioned aspect: they forced the hour. They thought they would rectify the world through selling Yosef, for they saw that he brought an evil report about them to their father and saw that Yaravam and Achav would issue from him. Therefore, according to their understanding, they wanted to kill him, and their intention was for the rectification of the world, so that Yaravam and Achav would not issue from him; and likewise their other mistaken reasonings about this. For they were certainly great righteous ones, but they erred greatly, and the principal blemish was in the aspect of forcing the hour, as stated above. This is why he reproved them: “Shimon and Levi are brothers; instruments of violence are their swords.” Specifically “instruments of violence”—the aspect of violence and robbery, which was their blemish; for one who forces the hour, even if he is righteous, is in the aspect of a robber and a violent extortioner, as stated above.

(Laws of Gizeyluh, law 5, item 10)

pairs.he: וְאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ בִּקֵּשׁ לְגַלּוֹת אֶת הַקֵּץ וְנִסְתַּלְּקָה הֵימֶנּוּ שְׁכִינָה, אָמַר, שֶׁמָּא יֵשׁ בֵּינֵיכֶם פָּסוּל כְּשֵׁם וְכוּ׳. מִיָּד פָּתְחוּ כֻּלָּם וְאָמְרוּ, שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל ה׳ אֱלֹקֵינוּ ה׳ אֶחָד, כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין בְּלִבְּךָ אֶלָּא אֶחָד כָּךְ אֵין בְּלִבֵּנוּ אֶלָּא אֶחָד. וְאָז הִתְחִיל לְדַבֵּר דְּבָרִים אֲחֵרִים וְקִנְטֵר אֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים רְאוּבֵן וְשִׁמְעוֹן וְכוּ׳. הַיְנוּ כִּי יַעֲקֹב עֵת שֶׁבַּתְּחִלָּה סָבַר שֶׁכְּבָר הִגִּיעַ הָעֵת לְגַלּוֹת לָהֶם אֶת הַקֵּץ וְנִסְתַּלְּקָה הֵימֶנּוּ שְׁכִינָה וְעַל כֵּן סָבַר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם אֵיזֶה פָּסוּל כַּנַּ״ל. כֵּיוָן שֶׁאָמְרוּ שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּ׳ וְרָאָה שֶׁכָּל הָעֵדָה כֻּלָּם קְדוֹשִׁים וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן נִסְתַּלְּקָה מִמֶּנּוּ שְׁכִינָה עַל שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ לְגַלּוֹת אֶת הַקֵּץ, שֶׁאָז הֵבִין מִיָּד שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִדְחֹק אֶת הַשָּׁעָה בְּשׁוּם דָּבָר, וּבִפְרָט בְּעִנְיַן הַקֵּץ הָאַחֲרוֹן לָשׁוּב לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְשֶׁתִּהְיֶה גְּאֻלָּה שְׁלֵמָה שֶׁאֵין אַחֲרֶיהָ גָּלוּת, שֶׁזֶּה נֶעְלָם מִכָּל הַצַּדִּיקִים הַגְּדוֹלִים וַאֲפִלּוּ הַצַּדִּיקִים הַיּוֹדְעִים בָּזֶה קְצָת אָסוּר לְגַלּוֹת כִּי לִבָּה לְפוּמָה לֹא גָּלֵי, וְאָז הֵבִין גֹּדֶל הַפְּגָם שֶׁל הַדּוֹחֵק אֶת הַשָּׁעָה אֲפִלּוּ צַדִּיקִים גְּדוֹלִים.
pairs.en: And our sages of blessed memory said that Yaakov our father wished to reveal the end, and the Divine Presence departed from him. He said: Perhaps there is an unfit one among you, just as, etc. Immediately they all began and said: “Hear, Israel: the Lord is our God; the Lord is one. Just as in your heart there is only one, so in our heart there is only one.” And then he began speaking of other matters and reproved the tribes, Reuven and Shimon, etc. That is, initially Yaakov thought that the time had already come to reveal the end to them, and the Divine Presence departed from him; and therefore he thought that there was some unfitness among them, as stated above. Once they said “Hear, Israel,” etc., and he saw that the whole congregation was entirely holy, yet nevertheless the Divine Presence had departed from him because he wished to reveal the end, then he immediately understood that it is impossible to force the hour in any matter. And especially concerning the final end—returning to the land of Israel and there being a complete redemption after which there is no exile—this is concealed from all the great righteous ones. And even the righteous who know a little about it are forbidden to reveal it, for the heart does not disclose it to the mouth. And then he understood the magnitude of the blemish of one who forces the hour—even great righteous ones.

qualifiedAfter.en: And our sages of blessed memory said that Yaakov our father wished to reveal the end, and the Divine Presence departed from him. pairs.he: וזה מה שהוכיח את ג׳ השבטים שזה היה הפגם שלהם בחינה זו של דוחק את השעה
pairs.en: And this is what he reproved the three tribes for: this was their blemish, this aspect of forcing the hour.

qualifiedAfter.he: וזה מה שהוכיח את ג׳ השבטים שזה היה הפגם שלהם בחינה זו של דוחק את השעה
qualifiedAfter.en: And this is what he reproved the three tribes for: this was their blemish, this aspect of forcing the hour.

pairs.he: וְעַל כֵּן אָז הִתְחִיל לְקַנְטֵר אֶת הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה שְׁבָטִים עַל פְּגָמֵיהֶם, וְעִקַּר הַפְּגָם שֶׁלָּהֶם הָיָה בְּעִנְיַן הַדּוֹחֵק אֶת הַשָּׁעָה. בְּחִינַת פַּחַז כַּמַּיִם אַל תּוֹתַר הַיְנוּ שֶׁבָּלְבַל בְּחִפָּזוֹן וּבֶהָלָה גְּדוֹלָה וּבִלְבֵּל יְצוּעֵי אָבִיו, וְעִקַּר הַפְּגָם הָיָה בִּבְחִינַת דּוֹחֵק אֶת הַשָּׁעָה בְּחִינַת פַּחַז כַּמַּיִם, כִּי רְאוּבֵן הָיָה בְּוַדַּאי צַדִּיק גָּדוֹל וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה, כָּל הָאוֹמֵר רְאוּבֵן חָטָא אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא טוֹעֶה. רַק שֶׁהַפְּגָם שֶׁלּוֹ הָיָה שֶׁקִּנֵּא קִנְאַת אִמּוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה וּבֶאֱמֶת גַּם זֶה הָיָה פְּגָם גָּדוֹל וְעִקַּר הַפְּגָם בִּבְחִינַת הַדּוֹחֵק אֶת הַשָּׁעָה.
pairs.en: Therefore he then began to reprove the three tribes concerning their blemishes, and the principal blemish they had was in the matter of forcing the hour. The aspect of “Hasty as water, you shall not have preeminence”: that is, he acted disruptively in haste and great agitation and disturbed his father’s couches; and the principal blemish was in the aspect of forcing the hour, the aspect of “Hasty as water.” For Reuven was certainly a great righteous man, and as our sages of blessed memory said: Anyone who says Reuven sinned is only mistaken. Rather, his blemish was that he was zealous for his mother’s cause, as our sages of blessed memory said. In truth, this too was a great blemish, and the principal blemish was in the aspect of forcing the hour.

In truth, this too was a great blemish, and the principal blemish was in the aspect of forcing the hour.

pairs.he: וּבָזֶה פּוֹגְמִים גַּם עַתָּה צַדִּיקִים וּכְשֵׁרִים וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי וְהֵבַנְתִּי מִפִּיו הַקָּדוֹשׁ זִכְרוֹ צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה שֶׁאָמַר, שֶׁזֶּה יֵצֶר הָרַע גָּדוֹל אֵצֶל כַּמָּה בְּנֵי אָדָם, וּבִפְרָט הַגְּדוֹלִים בְּמַעֲלָה שֶׁבִּשְׁבִיל דָּבָר אֶחָד שֶׁנִּדְמֶה לָהֶם שֶׁהוּא מִצְוָה הֵם מַפְקִירִים הַכֹּל וּבָאִים עַל יְדֵי זֶה לִידֵי קִלְקוּלִים רַבִּים וּבִפְרָט כְּשֶׁבָּאִים עַל יְדֵי זֶה לִידֵי מַחֲלֹקֶת. וּכְשֶׁנְּעַיֵּן בְּכָל הַמַּעֲשִׂיּוֹת שֶׁהָיָה בֵּין הַצַּדִּיקִים בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר הַכֹּל הָיָה בִּבְחִינָה זֹאת, שֶׁהַבַּעַל דָּבָר הִטְעָה אוֹתָם כְּאִלּוּ שֶׁכְּנֶגְדּוֹ פּוֹגֵם הַרְבֵּה וּמִצְוָה לִמְסֹר נֶפֶשׁ לְרָדְפוֹ וְכוּ׳.
pairs.en: And in this, even now righteous and upright people cause a blemish. And this is as I heard and understood from his holy mouth—may the memory of the righteous be for a blessing—when he said that this is a great evil inclination among several people, especially those of high standing: for the sake of one thing that seems to them to be a commandment, they abandon everything, and through this come to many corruptions, especially when through this they come into controversy. And when we examine all the episodes that occurred among the righteous in every generation, everything was in this aspect: the Baal Davar misled them, as though the person opposing him blemishes greatly and it were a commandment to give one’s life to pursue him, etc.

qualifiedAfter.en: And in this, even now righteous and upright people cause a blemish. pairs.he: וּבֶאֱמֶת שָׁגוּ בָּזֶה מְאֹד, כִּי עַל יְדֵי הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת וְהַכַּעַס אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְתַקֵּן בְּשׁוּם אֹפֶן רַק צְרִיכִין לְהִתְיַשֵּׁב הַרְבֵּה אֵיךְ לְהִתְנַהֵג בָּזֶה. וְהָעִקָּר לְבַקֵּשׁ מֵה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיַּנְחֵהוּ בְּדֶרֶךְ הָאֱמֶת וּלְהִתְיַשֵּׁב עַצְמוֹ הַרְבֵּה אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ כֹּחַ לְרָדְפוֹ, וְאוּלַי כַּוָּנָתוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁנִי לְשָׁמַיִם רַק שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהָבִין דְּבָרָיו. וְגַם אָמְרוּ עָלָיו הַרְבֵּה שְׁקָרִים וּכְזָבִים, בְּחִינַת אֲשֶׁר לֹא גָזַלְתִּי אָז אָשִׁיב. וְיֵשׁ בָּזֶה הַרְבֵּה לְדַבֵּר.
pairs.en: And in truth they erred greatly in this, for through controversy and anger it is impossible to rectify in any manner. Rather, one must deliberate greatly about how to conduct oneself in this. And the principal thing is to ask the blessed Lord to lead him in the way of truth, and to deliberate greatly whether he has the strength to pursue him. And perhaps the other person’s intention is for Heaven, but his words cannot be understood; and they also said many lies and falsehoods about him—the aspect of “What I did not steal, then I shall restore.” And there is much to say about this.

qualifiedAfter.en: And in truth they erred greatly in this, for through controversy and anger it is impossible to rectify in any manner. pairs.he: וְזֶה הָיָה בְּחִינַת הַפְּגָם שֶׁל רְאוּבֵן, שֶׁכַּוָּנָתוֹ בְּוַדַּאי לְשָׁמַיִם כִּי קִנֵּא קִנְאַת אִמּוֹ. אַף עַל פִּי כֵן פָּגַם בָּזֶה מְאֹד עַד שֶׁאָבַד עַל יְדֵי זֶה הַכְּהֻנָּה וְהַמַּלְכוּת וְכָל הַפְּגָם הָיָה בִּבְחִינַת דּוֹחֵק אֶת הַשָּׁעָה בְּחִינַת פַּחַז כַּמַּיִם אַל תּוֹתַר וְכוּ׳ כַּנַּ״ל:
pairs.en: This was the aspect of Reuven’s blemish: his intention was certainly for Heaven, for he was zealous for his mother’s cause. Nevertheless, he blemished this greatly, until through this he lost the priesthood and the kingship. The entire blemish was in the aspect of forcing the hour, the aspect of “Hasty as water, you shall not have preeminence,” etc., as stated above:

pairs.he: וּבִפְרָט שִׁמְעוֹן וְלֵוִי שָׁגוּ בָּזֶה הַרְבֵּה יוֹתֵר, כִּי מָכְרוּ אֶת יוֹסֵף שֶׁהַכֹּל הָיָה בִּבְחִינָה הַנַּ״ל שֶׁדָּחֲקוּ אֶת הַשָּׁעָה. וְסָבְרוּ שֶׁיְּתַקְּנוּ הָעוֹלָם עַל יְדֵי מְכִירַת יוֹסֵף, כִּי רָאוּ שֶׁמֵּבִיא אֶת דִּבָּתָם רָעָה אֶל אֲבִיהֶם וְרָאוּ שֶׁיָּצְאוּ מִמֶּנּוּ יָרָבְעָם וְאַחְאָב. עַל כֵּן לְפִי דַּעְתָּם רָצוּ לְהָרְגוֹ וְכַוָּנָתָם הָיָה בִּשְׁבִיל תִּקּוּן הָעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא יֵצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ יָרָבְעָם וְאַחְאָב וְכֵן שְׁאָרֵי סְבָרוֹת שֶׁל טָעוּת שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם בָּזֶה. כִּי בְּוַדַּאי הָיוּ צַדִּיקִים גְּדוֹלִים אַךְ שָׁגוּ הַרְבֵּה וְעִקַּר הַפְּגָם הָיָה בִּבְחִינַת דּוֹחֵק הַשָּׁעָה כַּנַּ״ל. וְזֶה שֶׁקִּנְטְרָם שִׁמְעוֹן וְלֵוִי אַחִים כְּלֵי חָמָס מְכֵרוֹתֵיהֶם. כְּלֵי חָמָס דַּיְקָא בְּחִינַת חָמָס וְגֶזֶל שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה הַפְּגָם שֶׁלָּהֶם, כִּי הַדּוֹחֵק אֶת הַשָּׁעָה אֲפִלּוּ אִם הוּא צַדִּיק הוּא בְּחִינַת גַּזְלָן וְחַמְסָן כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: Shimon and Levi in particular erred in this much more, for they sold Yosef, and all this was in the aforementioned aspect: they forced the hour. They thought they would rectify the world through selling Yosef, for they saw that he brought an evil report about them to their father and saw that Yaravam and Achav would issue from him. Therefore, according to their understanding, they wanted to kill him, and their intention was for the rectification of the world, so that Yaravam and Achav would not issue from him; and likewise their other mistaken reasonings about this. For they were certainly great righteous ones, but they erred greatly, and the principal blemish was in the aspect of forcing the hour, as stated above. segments.he:
הוכיח אותם שנמשכו אחר עצות לא טובות, שהרבה צריך לישב עצמו מה עצה נכונה

״פַּחַז כַּמַּיִם אַל תּוֹתַר״

(מ״ט, ד)

זֶה בְּחִינַת מַה שֶׁקִּנְטֵר הַשְּׁלֹשׁ שְׁבָטִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים עַל שֶׁנִּמְשְׁכוּ אַחַר עֲצוֹת לֹא טוֹבוֹת. וְאָמַר לִרְאוּבֵן ״פַּחַז כַּמַּיִם אַל תּוֹתַר״ וְכוּ׳. כִּי לֹא הָיְתָה עֲצָתוֹ טוֹבָה מַה שֶׁבִּלְבֵּל יְצוּעֵי אָבִיו, שֶׁנִּדְמָה לוֹ שֶׁהוּא עֵצָה טוֹבָה לִתְבֹּעַ עֶלְבּוֹן אִמּוֹ, אִם אֲחוֹת אִמִּי הָיְתָה צָרָה לְאִמִּי וְכוּ׳, אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת לֹא הָיְתָה טוֹבָה, כִּי צְרִיכִין לְיַשֵּׁב עַצְמוֹ הַרְבֵּה אִם לַעֲשׂוֹת דָּבָר כָּזֶה.

כִּי זֶה צְרִיכִין לֵידַע שֶׁהָעֵצָה הָאֲמִתִּיּוֹת לְהַצִּיל עַל יָדָהּ לָנֶצַח, צְרִיכִין לְיַשֵּׁב עַצְמוֹ הַרְבֵּה וּלְבַקֵּשׁ וּלְהִתְחַנֵּן הַרְבֵּה הַרְבֵּה לַה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה לְעֵצוֹת שְׁלֵמוֹת שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה עַל יָדָם לְאַחֲרִיתוֹ טוֹב. וְעַל כֵּן צָעַק דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, עַד אָנָה אָשִׁית עֵצוֹת בְּנַפְשִׁי וְכוּ׳. שֶׁמּוּבָן מִזֶּה שֶׁהָיָה חוֹשֵׁב כָּל יָמָיו עֵצוֹת הַרְבֵּה וְהָיָה קָשֶׁה לוֹ לָשׁוּת עֵצוֹת לְנַפְשׁוֹ, וְעַל כֵּן צָעַק עַד אָנָה אָשִׁית עֵצוֹת וְכוּ׳.

וְעַל כֵּן קִנְטְרוֹ, פַּחַז כַּמַּיִם וְכוּ׳, כִּי לֹא הָיָה לוֹ לְמַהֵר כָּל כָּךְ לְעֵצָה כָּזֹאת. וְכֵן קִנְטֵר שִׁמְעוֹן וְלֵוִי ״בְּסֹדָם״, הַיְנוּ בַּעֲצָתָם, ״אַל תָּבֹא נַפְשִׁי״, כִּי גַּם הֵם לֹא הָיְתָה עֲצָתָם יָפָה וְכוּ׳.

אֲבָל יְהוּדָה אַתָּה יוֹדוּךָ אַחֶיךָ וְכוּ׳, כִּי יְהוּדָה הוֹדָה וְלֹא בּוֹשׁ, שֶׁעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר ״אַתָּה יוֹדוּךָ אַחֶיךָ״. כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רבותינו זכרונם לברכה.

הַיְנוּ כִּי זֶה עִקַּר הָעֵצָה הָאֲמִתִּית שֶׁיּוֹדֶה עַל חֶטְאוֹ וְלֹא יֵבוֹשׁ, וִיבַקֵּשׁ תָּמִיד מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רַחֲמִים וְתַחֲנוּנִים שֶׁיִּמְחֹל לוֹ וִיתַקְּנֵהוּ בְּעֵצָה שְׁלֵמָה אֵיךְ לָשׁוּב אֵלָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁזֶּה הַדֶּרֶךְ הִתְחִיל יְהוּדָה עַל יְדֵי שֶׁעָמַד בְּנִסָּיוֹן בָּעֵת שֶׁאָמְרָה, הַכֶּר נָא וְכוּ׳, וְקִבֵּל עָלָיו עֶלְבּוֹן כָּזֶה, כִּי יָשְׁבוּ שָׁם שֵׁם וְעֵבֶר וְיִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב. כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רבותינו זכרונם לברכה. וְהוּא הוֹדָה וְלֹא בּוֹשׁ בִּפְנֵיהֶם. וְגָרַם לִרְאוּבֵן שֶׁיּוֹדֶה גַּם כֵּן. וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה בֶּאֱמֶת שֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנּוּ כָּל מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא מְשִׁיחַ מִזַּרְעוֹ.

שֶׁעִקַּר שְׁלֵמוּת הָעֵצָה עַל יָדוֹ כַּנַּ״ל, כִּי הוּא יַמְשִׁיךְ עֵצוֹת עֲמֻקּוֹת כָּאֵלֶּה בָּעוֹלָם עַד שֶׁיַּחֲזוֹר הַכֹּל בִּתְשׁוּבָה עַל יְדֵי זֶה. וְזֶה, ״יִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לְךָ בְּנֵי אָבִיךָ״, שֶׁכָּל הַמְּלוּכָה תָּשׁוּב לְבֵית דָּוִד שֶׁיִּתְאַחֲדוּ הַמַּלְכוּת בְּחִינַת וְלֹא יֵחָצוּ לִשְׁתֵּי מַמְלָכוֹת עוֹד, שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת הִתְאַחֲדוּת הָעֵצָה, דְּהַיְנוּ תִּקּוּן הָעֵצָה.

(הלכות תשעה באב ותעניות הלכה ד׳ אות ט״ו)
segments.en:
He reproved them for having been drawn after bad counsels, for one must deliberate greatly with oneself as to which counsel is correct.

“Unstable as water, you shall not excel.”

(49:4)

This is the aspect of his reproaching the first three tribes for having been drawn after bad counsels. And he said to Reuven, “Unstable as water, you shall not excel,” etc. For his counsel was not good when he disturbed his father’s couch; it seemed to him to be good counsel to demand redress for the insult to his mother: if my mother’s sister was a rival to my mother, etc. But in truth it was not good, for one must deliberate greatly with oneself as to whether to do such a thing.

For this one must know: for the true counsel through which one is saved for eternity, one must deliberate greatly with oneself, and petition and supplicate the blessed Lord exceedingly, exceedingly, that one merit complete counsels through which one will merit a good final end. Therefore King David, peace upon him, cried, “How long shall I set counsels in my soul,” etc. From this it is understood that throughout his days he thought of many counsels, and it was difficult for him to set counsels for his soul; therefore he cried, “How long shall I set counsels,” etc.

Therefore he reproached him, “Unstable as water,” etc., for he should not have hastened so much toward such counsel. And likewise he reproached Shimon and Levi: “Into their secret counsel”—that is, into their counsel—“let my soul not enter,” for their counsel also was not good, etc.

But “Yehudah, you—your brothers will acknowledge you,” etc., for Yehudah acknowledged and was not ashamed; concerning this it is said, “You—your brothers will acknowledge you,” as our sages of blessed memory said.

That is, this is the principal true counsel: that he acknowledge his sin and not be ashamed, and continually petition the blessed God for mercy and supplication, that He forgive him and rectify him with complete counsel as to how to return to Him, blessed be He. Yehudah began this path by withstanding the trial at the time she said, “Recognize, please,” etc., and accepting such humiliation upon himself; for Shem, Ever, Yitzchak, and Yaakov were sitting there, as our sages of blessed memory said. And he acknowledged and was not ashamed before them. He caused Reuven to acknowledge as well. And through this, indeed, the entire kingship of the house of David issued from him, until Messiah will come from his seed.

For the principal completeness of counsel is through him, as stated above, for he will draw such deep counsels into the world until all return in repentance through this. And this is “Your father’s sons will bow to you”: all sovereignty will return to the house of David, as the sovereignty becomes united, in the aspect of “and they shall no longer be divided into two kingdoms”; this is the aspect of the unification of counsel, that is, the rectification of counsel.

(Laws of Tishuh Bi’Av and Taaniyos, law 4, item 15)

pairs.he: כִּי זֶה צְרִיכִין לֵידַע שֶׁהָעֵצָה הָאֲמִתִּיּוֹת לְהַצִּיל עַל יָדָהּ לָנֶצַח, צְרִיכִין לְיַשֵּׁב עַצְמוֹ הַרְבֵּה וּלְבַקֵּשׁ וּלְהִתְחַנֵּן הַרְבֵּה הַרְבֵּה לַה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה לְעֵצוֹת שְׁלֵמוֹת שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה עַל יָדָם לְאַחֲרִיתוֹ טוֹב. וְעַל כֵּן צָעַק דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, עַד אָנָה אָשִׁית עֵצוֹת בְּנַפְשִׁי וְכוּ׳. שֶׁמּוּבָן מִזֶּה שֶׁהָיָה חוֹשֵׁב כָּל יָמָיו עֵצוֹת הַרְבֵּה וְהָיָה קָשֶׁה לוֹ לָשׁוּת עֵצוֹת לְנַפְשׁוֹ, וְעַל כֵּן צָעַק עַד אָנָה אָשִׁית עֵצוֹת וְכוּ׳.
pairs.en: For this one must know: for the true counsel through which one is saved for eternity, one must deliberate greatly with oneself, and petition and supplicate the blessed Lord exceedingly, exceedingly, that one merit complete counsels through which one will merit a good final end. Therefore King David, peace upon him, cried, “How long shall I set counsels in my soul,” etc. From this it is understood that throughout his days he thought of many counsels, and it was difficult for him to set counsels for his soul; therefore he cried, “How long shall I set counsels,” etc.

qualifiedAfter.en: For this one must know: for the true counsel through which one is saved for eternity, one must deliberate greatly with oneself, and petition and supplicate the blessed Lord exceedingly, exceedingly, that one merit complete counsels through which one will merit a good final end. Therefore King David, peace upon him, cried, “How long shall I set counsels in my soul,” etc. From this it is understood that throughout his days he thought of many counsels, and it was difficult for him to set counsels for his soul; therefore he cried, “How long shall I set counsels,” etc.

pairs.he: וְעַל כֵּן קִנְטְרוֹ, פַּחַז כַּמַּיִם וְכוּ׳, כִּי לֹא הָיָה לוֹ לְמַהֵר כָּל כָּךְ לְעֵצָה כָּזֹאת. וְכֵן קִנְטֵר שִׁמְעוֹן וְלֵוִי ״בְּסֹדָם״, הַיְנוּ בַּעֲצָתָם, ״אַל תָּבֹא נַפְשִׁי״, כִּי גַּם הֵם לֹא הָיְתָה עֲצָתָם יָפָה וְכוּ׳.
pairs.en: Therefore he reproached him, “Unstable as water,” etc., for he should not have hastened so much toward such counsel. And likewise he reproached Shimon and Levi: “Into their secret counsel”—that is, into their counsel—“let my soul not enter,” for their counsel also was not good, etc.

qualifiedAfter.en: Therefore he reproached him, “Unstable as water,” etc., for he should not have hastened so much toward such counsel. And likewise he reproached Shimon and Levi: “Into their secret counsel”—that is, into their counsel—“let my soul not enter,” for their counsel also was not good, etc.

pairs.he: אֲבָל יְהוּדָה אַתָּה יוֹדוּךָ אַחֶיךָ וְכוּ׳, כִּי יְהוּדָה הוֹדָה וְלֹא בּוֹשׁ, שֶׁעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר ״אַתָּה יוֹדוּךָ אַחֶיךָ״. כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רבותינו זכרונם לברכה.
pairs.en: But “Yehudah, you—your brothers will acknowledge you,” etc., for Yehudah acknowledged and was not ashamed; concerning this it is said, “You—your brothers will acknowledge you,” as our sages of blessed memory said.

qualifiedAfter.en: But “Yehudah, you—your brothers will acknowledge you,” etc., for Yehudah acknowledged and was not ashamed; concerning this it is said, “You—your brothers will acknowledge you,” as our sages of blessed memory said.

pairs.he: הַיְנוּ כִּי זֶה עִקַּר הָעֵצָה הָאֲמִתִּית שֶׁיּוֹדֶה עַל חֶטְאוֹ וְלֹא יֵבוֹשׁ, וִיבַקֵּשׁ תָּמִיד מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רַחֲמִים וְתַחֲנוּנִים שֶׁיִּמְחֹל לוֹ וִיתַקְּנֵהוּ בְּעֵצָה שְׁלֵמָה אֵיךְ לָשׁוּב אֵלָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁזֶּה הַדֶּרֶךְ הִתְחִיל יְהוּדָה עַל יְדֵי שֶׁעָמַד בְּנִסָּיוֹן בָּעֵת שֶׁאָמְרָה, הַכֶּר נָא וְכוּ׳, וְקִבֵּל עָלָיו עֶלְבּוֹן כָּזֶה, כִּי יָשְׁבוּ שָׁם שֵׁם וְעֵבֶר וְיִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב. כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רבותינו זכרונם לברכה. וְהוּא הוֹדָה וְלֹא בּוֹשׁ בִּפְנֵיהֶם. וְגָרַם לִרְאוּבֵן שֶׁיּוֹדֶה גַּם כֵּן. וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה בֶּאֱמֶת שֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנּוּ כָּל מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא מְשִׁיחַ מִזַּרְעוֹ.
pairs.en: That is, this is the principal true counsel: that he acknowledge his sin and not be ashamed, and continually petition the blessed God for mercy and supplication, that He forgive him and rectify him with complete counsel as to how to return to Him, blessed be He. Yehudah began this path by withstanding the trial at the time she said, “Recognize, please,” etc., and accepting such humiliation upon himself; for Shem, Ever, Yitzchak, and Yaakov were sitting there, as our sages of blessed memory said. And he acknowledged and was not ashamed before them. He caused Reuven to acknowledge as well. And through this, indeed, the entire kingship of the house of David issued from him, until Messiah will come from his seed.

qualifiedAfter.en: That is, this is the principal true counsel: that he acknowledge his sin and not be ashamed, and continually petition the blessed God for mercy and supplication, that He forgive him and rectify him with complete counsel as to how to return to Him, blessed be He. Yehudah began this path by withstanding the trial at the time she said, “Recognize, please,” etc., and accepting such humiliation upon himself; for Shem, Ever, Yitzchak, and Yaakov were sitting there, as our sages of blessed memory said. And he acknowledged and was not ashamed before them. He caused Reuven to acknowledge as well. And through this, indeed, the entire kingship of the house of David issued from him, until Messiah will come from his seed.

pairs.he: שֶׁעִקַּר שְׁלֵמוּת הָעֵצָה עַל יָדוֹ כַּנַּ״ל, כִּי הוּא יַמְשִׁיךְ עֵצוֹת עֲמֻקּוֹת כָּאֵלֶּה בָּעוֹלָם עַד שֶׁיַּחֲזוֹר הַכֹּל בִּתְשׁוּבָה עַל יְדֵי זֶה. וְזֶה, ״יִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לְךָ בְּנֵי אָבִיךָ״, שֶׁכָּל הַמְּלוּכָה תָּשׁוּב לְבֵית דָּוִד שֶׁיִּתְאַחֲדוּ הַמַּלְכוּת בְּחִינַת וְלֹא יֵחָצוּ לִשְׁתֵּי מַמְלָכוֹת עוֹד, שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת הִתְאַחֲדוּת הָעֵצָה, דְּהַיְנוּ תִּקּוּן הָעֵצָה.
pairs.en: For the principal completeness of counsel is through him, as stated above, for he will draw such deep counsels into the world until all return in repentance through this. And this is “Your father’s sons will bow to you”: all sovereignty will return to the house of David, as the sovereignty becomes united, in the aspect of “and they shall no longer be divided into two kingdoms”; this is the aspect of the unification of counsel, that is, the rectification of counsel.

qualifiedAfter.en: For the principal completeness of counsel is through him, as stated above, for he will draw such deep counsels into the world until all return in repentance through this. And this is “Your father’s sons will bow to you”: all sovereignty will return to the house of David, as the sovereignty becomes united, in the aspect of “and they shall no longer be divided into two kingdoms”; this is the aspect of the unification of counsel, that is, the rectification of counsel.

segments.he:
יעקב זכה להעמיד י״ב שבטים שכל אחד דעתו משונה מחברו וכולם הכירו באחדות ה׳ יתברך, שזה עיקר השלימות שיוכר האחדות מפעולות משתנות

״הִקָּבְצוּ וְשִׁמְעוּ בְּנֵי יַעֲקֹב״

(מ״ט, ב)

עִקַּר הִתְגַּלּוּת אַחְדוּת הַפָּשׁוּט מִתּוֹךְ פְּעֻלּוֹת מִשְׁתַּנּוֹת הָיָה עַל יְדֵי יַעֲקֹב, שֶׁזָּכָה לְהַעֲמִיד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שְׁבָטִים שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד הָיָה לוֹ דֵּעָה מְיֻחֶדֶת, כִּי כָּל אֶחָד מֵהַשְּׁבָטִים הָיָה גּוֹן מְיֻחָד כְּפִי גּוֹן אַבְנוֹ שֶׁבַּחֹשֶׁן, הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת פְּעֻלָּה מְשֻׁנָּה מֵחֲבֵרוֹ. וְכֻלָּם כְּאֶחָד נִכְלְלוּ בְּדֵעָה אַחַת וְאָמְרוּ כְּפֶה אֶחָד בִּשְׁעַת הִסְתַּלְּקוּת יַעֲקֹב שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל ה׳ אֱלֹקֵינוּ ה׳ אֶחָד. שֶׁזֶּה עִקַּר שְׁלֵמוּת הִתְגַּלּוּת אַחְדוּת הַפָּשׁוּט כְּשֶׁרַבִּים מַסְכִּימִים לְדֵעָה אַחַת, כַּמְבֹאָר בְּהַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּים, עַיֵּן שָׁם.

כִּי אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק שֶׁבִּימֵיהֶם לֹא נִתְבָּרֵר בִּשְׁלֵמוּת עֲדַיִן קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל כֵּן לֹא זָכָה כָּל אֶחָד לְהַעֲמִיד כִּי אִם בֵּן אֶחָד בִּקְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּהַיְנוּ אַבְרָהָם הֶעֱמִיד יִצְחָק לְבַדּוֹ, וְיִצְחָק אֶת יַעֲקֹב לְבַדּוֹ. וּבֵן הַשֵּׁנִי שֶׁהָיָה לְאַבְרָהָם שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ דֵּעָה מְשֻׁנָּה בְּוַדַּאי כִּי אֵין דּוֹמֶה דֵּעַת אָדָם אֶחָד לַחֲבֵרוֹ. וְתֵכֶף שֶׁהִגִּיעַ הָאֱמוּנָה לִשְׁנֵי דֵּעוֹת נֶאֱחַז זֻהֲמַת הַנָּחָשׁ בְּיִשְׁמָעֵאל שֶׁהָיָה בְּחִינַת פְּעֻלָּה מְשֻׁנָּה דֵּעָה מְשֻׁנָּה מִיִּצְחָק עַד שֶׁלֹּא זָכָה לַהֲפֹךְ דַּעְתּוֹ הַמְּשֻׁנָּה לְהִכָּלֵל בְּאַחְדוּת הַפָּשׁוּט. וְכֵן עֵשָׂו שֶׁהָיָה מְשֻׁנָּה מִיַּעֲקֹב לֹא זָכָה לְהִכָּלֵל עִם יַעֲקֹב בְּדֵעָה אַחַת, לְעִנְיַן עִקַּר יְסוֹד הָאֱמוּנָה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה, כִּי אָז לֹא נִתְבָּרֵר הַזֻּהֲמָא בִּשְׁלֵמוּת עַד שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה בִּשְׁלֵמוּת בְּחִינַת אַחְדוּת הַפָּשׁוּט מִתּוֹךְ פְּעֻלּוֹת מִשְׁתַּנּוֹת, דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁכָּל הַשִּׁנּוּי דֵּעוֹת יַסְכִּימוּ עַל עִקַּר יְסוֹד הָאֱמֶת וְהָאֱמוּנָה לְהַאֲמִין שֶׁכָּל הַפְּעֻלּוֹת מִשְׁתַּנּוֹת וְכָל הַשִּׁנּוּי דֵּעוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם כֻּלָּם נִמְשָׁכִין מֵאַחְדוּת הַפָּשׁוּט.

אֲבָל יַעֲקֹב זָכָה לָזֶה בִּשְׁלֵמוּת, כִּי זָכָה לְהַעֲמִיד בָּנִים הַרְבֵּה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שְׁבָטִים שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד הָיָה לוֹ דֵּעָה מְשֻׁנָּה, כִּי הָיָה בְּחִינַת גּוֹן מְיֻחָד בְּחִינַת פְּעֻלָּה מְשֻׁנָּה. וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן לְעִנְיַן יְסוֹד הָאֱמוּנָה כֻּלָּם הִסְכִּימוּ לְדֵעָה אַחַת וְאָמְרוּ כְּפֶה אֶחָד שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּ׳ ה׳ אֶחָד, שֶׁזֶּה עִקַּר שְׁלֵמוּת הִתְגַּלּוּת אַחְדוּת הַפָּשׁוּט כְּשֶׁרַבִּים שֶׁמְּשֻׁנִּים בְּדֵעוֹתֵיהֶם מַסְכִּימִים לְדֵעָה אַחַת.

(הלכות כלאי בהמה הלכה ד׳ אות ג׳)
segments.en:
Yaakov merited establishing twelve tribes, each of whose understanding differs from his fellow’s, and all recognized the unity of the blessed Lord; this is the principal completeness, that unity should be recognized from varying actions.

“Gather together and listen, sons of Yaakov.”

(49:2)

The principal revelation of simple unity from varying actions was through Yaakov, who merited establishing twelve tribes, each and every one of whom had a distinct understanding. For each of the tribes had a distinct color, according to the color of his stone in the breastplate—that is, the aspect of an action differing from his fellow’s. And all were included together in one understanding and said with one mouth at the time of Yaakov’s departure, “Hear, Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one.” This is the principal completeness of the revelation of simple unity, when many agree upon one understanding, as explained in this discourse: this is the aspect of the law following the many. See there.

For Avraham and Yitzchak—in whose days the holiness of Israel had not yet been completely clarified—each therefore merited establishing only one son in the holiness of Israel: Avraham established Yitzchak alone, and Yitzchak, Yaakov alone. And as for the second son whom Avraham had, who certainly had a differing understanding, since the understanding of one person is not like his fellow’s—as soon as faith reached two understandings, the serpent’s filth took hold in Yishmael, who was the aspect of a differing action, a differing understanding from Yitzchak, to the point that he did not merit turning his differing understanding to be included in simple unity. Likewise Esav, who differed from Yaakov, did not merit being included with Yaakov in one understanding concerning the principal foundation of holy faith, for then the filth had not been completely clarified until the aspect of simple unity from varying actions was completely revealed. That is, all the variation of understandings should agree upon the principal foundation of truth and faith: to believe that all the varying actions and all the variation of understandings in the world are drawn from simple unity.

But Yaakov merited this completely, for he merited establishing many sons, twelve tribes, each of whom had a differing understanding, because he was the aspect of a distinct color, the aspect of a differing action. Nevertheless, concerning the foundation of faith, they all agreed upon one understanding and said with one mouth, “Hear, Israel,” etc., “the Lord is one.” This is the principal completeness of the revelation of simple unity, when many who differ in their understandings agree upon one understanding.

(Laws of Kilay Bihaymuh, law 4, item 3)

segments.he:
התנבא על ריבוי הספרים והמצאת הדפוס שעל ידי זה יתרבו ספרים אין קץ סמוך לביאת משיח וכולם נצרכים לעולם להתקרב ע״י להקב״ה

״לֹא יָסוּר שֵׁבֶט מִיהוּדָה וּמְחֹקֵק מִבֵּין רַגְלָיו עַד כִּי יָבֹא שִׁילֹה״ (מט, י)

זֶה בְּחִינַת הַדְּפוּס שֶׁחָמַל עָלֵינוּ ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּאַחֲרִית הַיָּמִים וְהִמְצִיא בָּעוֹלָם חָכְמַת הַדְּפוּס כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְרַבּוּ סְפָרִים קְדוֹשִׁים בָּעוֹלָם. כִּי אָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (גיטין ס) דְּבָרִים שֶׁבִּכְתָב אִי אַתָּה רַשַּׁאי לְאָמְרָם בְּעַל פֶּה, דְּבָרִים שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה אִי אַתָּה רַשַּׁאי לְאָמְרָם בִּכְתָב. כִּי כְּבָר מְבֹאָר שֶׁתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה זֶה בְּחִינַת מֹשֶׁה, וְדָוִד בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה וּתְפִלָּה שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת מַחֲשָׁבָה וְדִבּוּר, שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת הַזִּכָּרוֹן וְהָאַזְהָרָה שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה, וְהַהִתְגַּבְּרוּת לְנַצֵּחַ הַמִּלְחָמָה, שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת דָּוִד כַּנַּ״ל. וּשְׁנֵי הַבְּחִינוֹת הָאֵלּוּ כָּל אֶחָד צָרִיךְ לַחֲבֵרוֹ וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָאֶחָד בְּלֹא חֲבֵרוֹ כַּנַּ״ל.

וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם צְרִיכִין. וְעִקַּר שְׁלֵמוּת הַתּוֹרָה עַל יְדֵי שְׁנֵיהֶם דַּיְקָא, וְאֵין אֶחָד בְּלֹא חֲבֵרוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר. ״מִשְׁפְּטֵי ה׳ אֱמֶת צָדְקוּ יַחְדָּו״, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁפֵּרֵשׁ רַשִׁ״י שָׁם, עַיֵּן שָׁם. כִּי תוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב בְּלֹא שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה אֵין לָהּ שׁוּם שְׁלֵמוּת. כִּי אֵין יוֹדְעִין שׁוּם דִּין וְאֵיךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת שׁוּם מִצְוָה בְּלֹא תוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה. וְכֵן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בְּלֹא תוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב גַּם כֵּן אֵינוֹ שְׁלֵמוּת. כִּי כָּל עִקַּר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה נִסְמָךְ עַל תוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, כִּי תוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הִיא פֵּרוּשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב. כִּי לֵיכָּא מִלְּתָא דְּלָא רְמִיזָא בְּאוֹרַיְתָא.

וְעִקַּר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב הוּא בְּחִינַת זִכָּרוֹן כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״כְּתֹב זֹאת זִכָּרוֹן בַּסֵּפֶר״, הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת הָאַזְהָרוֹת הַנַּ״ל שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַזִּכָּרוֹן שֶׁמַּזְכִּיר וּמַזְהִיר אֶת כָּל אֵיבַר הַמִּצְווֹת הַתְּלוּיוֹת בּוֹ כַּנַּ״ל. וְעַל כֵּן הוּא בִּכְתָב, כִּי הוּא עִקַּר הַזִּכָּרוֹן בִּכְתָב, כִּי בְּעַל פֶּה יְכוֹלִין לִשְׁכֹּחַ לְגַמְרֵי, וְעַל כֵּן צְרִיכִין לְכָתְבָהּ דַּיְקָא כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְקַיֵּם הַזִּכָּרוֹן שֶׁהוּא עַל יְדֵי כְּתָב דַּיְקָא. וְעַל כֵּן דְּבָרִים שֶׁבִּכְתָב אִי אַתָּה רַשַּׁאי לְאָמְרָם בְּעַל פֶּה, כִּי עִקַּר הָאַזְהָרָה וְהַזִּכָּרוֹן הוּא עַל יְדֵי כְּתָב כַּנַּ״ל, אֲבָל דְּבָרִים שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה צְרִיכִין לוֹמַר בְּעַל פֶּה דַּיְקָא וְאָסוּר לְאָמְרָם בִּכְתָב. כִּי תוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת לָבוֹא לִידֵי מַעֲשֶׂה כַּנַּ״ל, שֶׁזֶּה אִי אֶפְשָׁר כִּי אִם עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבּוּר פֶּה, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַדִּבּוּר פֶּה בִּקְדֻשָּׁה, מְהַפְּכִין הַגְּבוּרוֹת לַחֲסָדִים וְכוּ׳, שֶׁזֶּה עִקַּר נִצְחוֹן הַמִּלְחָמָה וְכוּ׳ כַּנַּ״ל. וְעַל כֵּן צְרִיכִין לְאָמְרָם בְּעַל פֶּה דַּיְקָא וְאָסוּר לְאָמְרָם בִּכְתָב, כִּי הַכְּתָב הוּא רַק בִּשְׁבִיל זִכָּרוֹן.

אֲבָל קָשֶׁה לָבוֹא לִידֵי מַעֲשֶׂה עַל יְדֵי הַכְּתָב, כִּי אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְבָאֵר בִּכְתָב כָּל פְּרָטֵי הַמִּצְווֹת וְדִקְדּוּקֶיהָ וְכָל דַּרְכֵי הָעֲשִׂיּוֹת וְהַדְּרָכִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ בַּעֲבוֹדַת הַבּוֹרֵא יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּי הַיֵּצֶר הָרַע וְחֵילוֹתָיו שֶׁאוֹחֲזִין בַּעֲכִירוּת הַדָּמִים, מִתְגַּבְּרִין מְאֹד בְּכָל אָדָם וּמְבַלְבְּלִין דַּעְתּוֹ הַרְבֵּה וּמִתְגַּבְּרִין לַהֲפֹךְ הָאֱמֶת, וְעַל כֵּן אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְבָרֵר בִּכְתָב הַכֹּל, כִּי דְּבָרִים הַנִּכְתָּבִין בַּסֵּפֶר אֶפְשָׁר לְהַטּוֹתָם מִן הָאֱמֶת וּלְפָרְשָׁם כִּרְצוֹנוֹ. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּמְצָא כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה שֶׁהָפְכוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹקִים חַיִּים וּפֵרְשׁוּ הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב פֵּרוּשִׁים זָרִים, שֶׁלֹּא כְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה וְגִלּוּ פָּנִים בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁלֹּא כַּהֲלָכָה וּבָאוּ לִידֵי כְּפִירוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת עַל יְדֵי פֵּרוּשֵׁיהֶם הַזָּרִים, כִּי בִּכְתָב אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְבָרֵר הָאֱמֶת לְתַכְלִיתוֹ, כִּי כָּל אֶחָד יָכוֹל לְפָרֵשׁ הַדְּבָרִים הַנִּכְתָּבִים כִּרְצוֹנוֹ.

וְעַל כֵּן נָתַן לָנוּ ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ כָּל דִּינֵי הַתּוֹרָה וּפֵרוּשֶׁיהָ בְּעַל פֶּה, כִּי מִפֶּה אֶל פֶּה יְכוֹלִין לְבָאֵר וּלְפָרֵשׁ הֵיטֵב הָאֱמֶת לַאֲמִתּוֹ כָּל דִּינֵי הַתּוֹרָה וּדְרָכֶיהָ וַעֲצוֹתֶיהָ לַאֲמִתָּן, אֲבָל בְּעַל פֶּה לְבַד בְּלֹא הַכְּתָב גַּם כֵּן אֵינוֹ שְׁלֵמוּת, כִּי בְּעַל פֶּה אֵין לוֹ יְסוֹד וְזִכָּרוֹן וּבְרַבּוֹת הַיָּמִים הָיָה יָכוֹל, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, לְהִשְׁתַּכֵּחַ לְגַמְרֵי. וְעַל כֵּן צְרִיכִין שְׁנֵיהֶם, בִּכְתָב וּבְעַל פֶּה בִּפְרָט, כְּדֵי לִשְׁמֹר הָאַזְהָרָה וְהַזִּכָּרוֹן, כִּי דְּבָרִים הַנִּכְתָּבִים מִתְקַיְּמִים לְעוֹלָם. וּבְעַל פֶּה צְרִיכִים כְּדֵי לְבָאֵר אֲמִתַּת הַדִּינִים וְדַרְכֵי הַתּוֹרָה הֵיטֵב בֶּאֱמֶת לַאֲמִתּוֹ, שֶׁזֶּה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְבָאֵר כִּי אִם עַל פֶּה דַּיְקָא.

אֲבָל בְּרַבּוֹת הַיָּמִים כְּשֶׁהִתְגַּבְּרוּ הַגָּלוּת וְחָשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁתַּכַּח הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, עַל כֵּן הִתִּירוּ לִכְתֹּב גַּם תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, מִשּׁוּם עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת לַה׳ הֵפֵרוּ תּוֹרָתֶךָ, כִּי רָאוּ שֶׁחֲשַׁשׁ הַשִּׁכְחָה גָּרוּעַ יוֹתֵר מֵהַחֲשַׁשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בִּכְתִיבָה, שֶׁלֹּא יְפָרְשׁוּהָ כִּרְצוֹנָם, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, כִּי הַחֲשָׁשָׁא שֶׁל שִׁכְחָה גָּרוּעַ יוֹתֵר. וְעַל כֵּן הִתִּירוּ לִכְתֹּב גַּם תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, אַךְ כְּשֶׁכּוֹתְבִין תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה צְרִיכִין לִכְתֹּב הַרְבֵּה מְאֹד מְאֹד כְּדֵי לְבָאֵר וּלְפָרֵשׁ הֵיטֵב הָאֱמֶת לַאֲמִתּוֹ, כִּי דְּבָרִים הַנִּכְתָּבִים בַּסֵּפֶר יָכוֹל הַקּוֹרֵא לְפָרְשָׁם כִּרְצוֹנוֹ כַּנַּ״ל, עַל כֵּן צְרִיכִין לְבָאֵר וּלְפָרֵשׁ הַדָּבָר הֵיטֵב בְּכַמָּה פֵּרוּשִׁים וּבֵאוּרִים, וּפֵרוּשׁ לְפֵרוּשִׁים כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל הַטּוֹעֶה לִטְעוֹת מֵהַפֵּרוּשׁ וְהַכַּוָּנָה הָאֲמִתִּית.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָנוּ רוֹאִין שֶׁמִּיּוֹם שֶׁהִתְחִילוּ לִכְתֹּב תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה נִתְרַבּוּ סְפָרִים הַרְבֵּה מְאֹד בָּעוֹלָם, כִּי לָא סַגִּי בְּלָאו הָכִי כַּנַּ״ל, בִּפְרָט שֶׁבְּכָל פַּעַם נִתְמַעֲטִין הַלְּבָבוֹת וְנֶחֱלָשִׁין הַדֵּעוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה, וַאֲנַן כְּסִיכְתָא בְּגוּדָא לִגְמָרָא וְכוּ׳, עַיֵּן שָׁם בְּעֵרוּבִין. וּכְמְבֹאָר בְּכָל סִפְרֵי הַמְחַבְּרִים, וְעַל כֵּן צְרִיכִין בְּכָל פַּעַם סְפָרִים הַרְבֵּה לְפָרֵשׁ כַּוָּנַת דִּבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה הֵיטֵב.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָנוּ רוֹאִין שֶׁהָרִי״ף קִצֵּר פִּסְקֵי הַגְּמָרָא בִּסְפָרָיו הַקְּדוֹשִׁים. וְאַחַר כֵּן נִתְרַבּוּ הַסְּפָרִים לְבָאֵר וּלְפָרֵשׁ דְּבָרָיו, אוֹ לַחֲלֹק עַל דְּבָרָיו בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁלֹּא נִרְאוּ לָהֶם דְּבָרָיו, וְאַחַר כֵּן נִתְחַבְּרוּ סְפָרִים עַל נוֹשְׂאֵי כֵּלָיו שֶׁל הָרִי״ף. וְכֵן בִּשְׁאָר סְפָרִים וְכוּ׳. וְכֻלָּם צְרִיכִים לְהָעוֹלָם מְאֹד וְאִם לֹא הָיוּ אֵלּוּ הַסְּפָרִים לֹא הָיִינוּ יוֹדְעִים עַתָּה שׁוּם דִּין.

וְכֵן בְּדַרְכֵי מוּסָר וְיִרְאָה וַעֲצוֹת וּדְרָכִים לַעֲבוֹדַת הַבּוֹרֵא יִתְבָּרַךְ מִתְרַבִּין בְּכָל פַּעַם סְפָרִים קְדוֹשִׁים הַלָּלוּ כְּדֵי לְבָאֵר וּלְגַלּוֹת לָנוּ הֵיטֵב אֲמִתַּת הַדְּרָכִים וְהָעֵצוֹת לִזְכּוֹת לַעֲבוֹדַת הַבּוֹרֵא יִתְבָּרַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת. וְכָל מַה שֶּׁמִּתְאָרֵךְ הַגָּלוּת יוֹתֵר, בַּעֲווֹנוֹתֵינוּ הָרַבִּים, וְנִתְמַעֲטִין הַלְּבָבוֹת צְרִיכִין בְּכָל פַּעַם סְפָרִים הַרְבֵּה יוֹתֵר כְּדֵי לְבָאֵר אֲמִתַּת הַכַּוָּנָה הֵיטֵב, לְשַׁבֵּר מַלְתְּעוֹת עָוֶל, לְהוֹצִיא מִלִּבָּן שֶׁל הַטּוֹעִים וְהַכּוֹפְרִים שֶׁלֹּא יוּכְלוּ לַהֲפֹךְ וּלְהַטּוֹתָם מִן הָאֱמֶת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.

עַל כֵּן בְּרַבּוֹת הַיָּמִים שֶׁרָאָה ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהַגָּלוּת מִתְגַּבֵּר בְּיוֹתֵר וְהַלְּבָבוֹת נִתְמַעֲטִין מְאֹד מְאֹד וּצְרִיכִין סְפָרִים הַרְבֵּה מְאֹד, עַל כֵּן חָמַל ה׳ עַל עַמּוֹ וְסִבֵּב בְּרַחֲמָיו הַנִּפְלָאִים וְהִמְצִיא בָּעוֹלָם חָכְמַת מְלֶאכֶת הַדְּפוּס כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְרַבּוּ סְפָרִים הַרְבֵּה בָּעוֹלָם, כִּי כְּפִי רִבּוּי הַסְּפָרִים שֶׁל אֵלּוּ הַדּוֹרוֹת לֹא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לְכָתְבָם בְּשׁוּם אֹפֶן וּבֶאֱמֶת אָנוּ צְרִיכִין כֻּלָּם, כִּי בְּוַדַּאי אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָנוּ עַתָּה לֵידַע דִּינֵי הַתּוֹרָה עַל בֻּרְיָן, כִּי אִם כְּשֶׁיִּהְיֶה לָנוּ סִפְרֵי הַשַּׁ״ס עִם פֵּרוּשׁ רַשִׁ״י וְהוֹסָפוֹת וּמְהַרְשָׁ״א וּשְׁאָר מְפָרְשִׁים, וְסִפְרֵי הָרִי״ף עִם כָּל הַפֵּרוּשִׁים. וְסִפְרֵי הָרֹא״שׁ וְהָרַמְבַּ״ם וְנוֹשְׂאֵי כֵּלָיו, וְהַטּוּר וּמְפָרְשָׁיו, וְסִפְרֵי הָאַחֲרוֹנִים, הַבֵּית יוֹסֵף וְהָרְמָ״א וְנוֹשְׂאֵי כֵּלֵיהֶם וְכוּ׳ וְסִפְרֵי שְׁאֵלוֹת וּתְשׁוּבוֹת וְכוּ׳, שֶׁבְּכָל אֵלּוּ מִשְׁתַּמְּשִׁים הַגְּדוֹלִים בְּסִפְרֵי תְּשׁוּבוֹתֵיהֶם כְּשֶׁרוֹצִים לְבָרֵר לָנוּ דִּין לַאֲמִתּוֹ. וּבִלְעֲדֵי כָּל הַסְּפָרִים הַנַּ״ל וְיוֹתֵר מֵהֶם, אִי אֶפְשָׁר עַתָּה לְבָרֵר הַדִּין לַאֲמִתּוֹ. וְכֵן בְּדַרְכֵי עֲצוֹת וּמוּסָר בַּעֲבוֹדַת ה׳, שֶׁצְּרִיכִין כָּל סִפְרֵי הַמִּדְרָשִׁים וּפֵרוּשֵׁיהֶם וְסִפְרֵי הַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ וְכִתְבֵי הָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה, וְרֵאשִׁית חָכְמָה וְכוּ׳ וְכוּ׳.

עַל כֵּן מַה יָּקְרוּ חַסְדֵי ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ אֲשֶׁר חָמַל עָלֵינוּ וְנָתַן לָנוּ מְלֶאכֶת הַדְּפוּס, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְרַבִּין הַסְּפָרִים וּבְנָקֵל בְּזוֹל גָּדוֹל. וְיֵשׁ סְפָרִים הַרְבֵּה בְּכָל עִיר וְאֵצֶל כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְקַיֶּמֶת הַתּוֹרָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל עַתָּה, כִּי כְּשֶׁכּוֹתְבִין תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה צְרִיכִין לִכְתֹּב הַרְבֵּה מְאֹד כְּדֵי לְבָאֵר הָאֱמֶת לַאֲמִתּוֹ. וּבְכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר שֶׁמִּתְמַעֲטִין הַלְּבָבוֹת יוֹתֵר צְרִיכִין לְבָאֵר יוֹתֵר וּצְרִיכִין לְהַרְבּוֹת בִּסְפָרִים קְדוֹשִׁים יוֹתֵר. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַבֵּנוּ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה (בסימן סא), שֶׁכְּבָר יֵשׁ הַרְבֵּה סְפָרִים וְעוֹד עֲתִידִים לִהְיוֹת הַרְבֵּה סְפָרִים, וְכֻלָּם צְרִיכִים לְהָעוֹלָם מְאֹד וְאָסוּר לְהַלְעִיג עַל אֶחָד מֵהֶם וְכוּ׳. וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וְיוֹתֵר מֵהֵמָּה בְּנִי הִזָּהֵר עֲשׂוֹת סְפָרִים הַרְבֵּה אֵין קֵץ״, וּפֵרֵשׁ רַשִׁ״י, ״יוֹתֵר מִמַּה שֶׁנִּכְתָּב, ׳הִזָּהֵר׳ לְקַיֵּם דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים בְּעַל פֶּה. וְאִם תֹּאמַר, לָמָּה לֹא נִכְתְּבוּ, עֲשׂוֹת סְפָרִים הַרְבֵּה אֵין קֵץ, אִם בָּאנוּ לִכְתֹּב לֹא הִסְפַּקְנוּ, הַיְנוּ כַּנַּ״ל שֶׁדְּבָרִים שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה אִם רוֹצִים לְכָתְבָם צְרִיכִים לִכְתֹּב הַרְבֵּה מְאֹד כַּנַּ״ל.

עַל כֵּן הוּא חֶסֶד גָּדוֹל מְלֶאכֶת הַדְּפוּס, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה יְכוֹלִים לְהַדְפִּיס סְפָרִים הַרְבֵּה מְאֹד כַּנַּ״ל, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה לֹא תִּשְׁתַּכַּח הַתּוֹרָה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל וְכַנַּ״ל.

וְעַל זֶה הִתְנַבֵּא יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ כְּשֶׁבֵּרַךְ אֶת יְהוּדָה שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ יָצָא הַמָּשִׁיחַ, ״לֹא יָסוּר שֵׁבֶט מִיהוּדָה וּמְחֹקֵק מִבֵּין רַגְלָיו עַד כִּי יָבֹא שִׁילֹה״. מְחֹקֵק זֶה הַדְּפוּס שֶׁהִתְנַבֵּא שֶׁלֹּא יָסוּר שֵׁבֶט מִיהוּדָה זֶה בְּחִינַת שֵׁבֶט סוֹפֵר, בְּחִינַת כְּתִיבַת הַסְּפָרִים הַקְּדוֹשִׁים שֶׁל הַתּוֹרָה, ׳וּמְחֹקֵק׳ זֶה בְּחִינַת הַדְּפוּס, שֶׁתִּתְגַּלֶּה חָכְמַת הַדְּפוּס בָּעוֹלָם וְלֹא תִּתְבַּטֵּל חֲקִיקַת וְהַדְפָּסַת סִפְרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, ׳עַד כִּי יָבֹא שִׁילֹה׳ דָּא מָשִׁיחַ, כִּי עַל יְדֵי רִבּוּי הַסְּפָרִים הַקְּדוֹשִׁים, עַל יְדֵי חָכְמַת הַדְּפוּס לֹא תִּשְׁתַּכַּח הַתּוֹרָה עַד שֶׁיָּבוֹא שִׁילֹה דָּא מֹשֶׁה מָשִׁיחַ.

וְזֶה ׳וְלוֹ יִקְּהַת עַמִּים אֹסְרִי לַגֶּפֶן עִירֹה וְכוּ׳ כִּבֵּס בַּיַּיִן וְכוּ׳ חַכְלִילִי עֵינַיִם מִיָּיִן וְכוּ׳, כִּי לֶעָתִיד כְּשֶׁיָּבוֹא מָשִׁיחַ אָז יִכָּלְלוּ מֹשֶׁה וְדָוִד בְּיַחַד בְּתַכְלִית הָאַחְדוּת, כִּי שִׁילֹה דָּא מֹשֶׁה, שֶׁהוּא מָשִׁיחַ. וְכֵן דָּוִד הוּא מָשִׁיחַ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״מְשִׁיחַ אֱלֹקֵי יַעֲקֹב״, כִּי נִשְׁמַת מָשִׁיחַ יִהְיֶה כָּלוּל מִשְּׁנֵיהֶם, מִמֹּשֶׁה וְדָוִד, וְאָז תִּהְיֶה הַגְּאֻלָּה שְׁלֵמָה שֶׁאֵין אַחֲרֶיהָ גָּלוּת, כִּי נִזְכֶּה לִזְכֹּר הָאַזְהָרוֹת שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה וּלְקַיְּמָם בִּשְׁלֵמוּת עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת דָּוִד. כִּי שְׁנֵיהֶם, מֹשֶׁה וְדָוִד יִכָּלְלוּ בְּיַחַד. וְזֶה בְּחִינַת עַד כִּי יָבֹא שִׁילֹה וְלוֹ יִקְּהַת עַמִּים, שֶׁכָּל הָעַמִּים, שֶׁהֵם הַשִּׁבְעִים אֻמּוֹת, יִתְהַפְּכוּ אֶל הַקְּדֻשָּׁה וְיִתְאַסְּפוּ כֻּלָּם אֶל מֹשֶׁה מָשִׁיחַ, שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת הַנַּ״ל, שֶׁהַדָּמִים נִכְלָלִין בַּקְּדֻשָּׁה, שֶׁשְּׂמֹאל נִכְלָל בְּיָמִין וְכוּ׳ כַּנַּ״ל, שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת הַיַּיִן דִּקְדֻשָּׁה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת דָּוִד כַּנַּ״ל.

וְזֶה שֶׁנִּסְמָךְ מִיָּד, אֹסְרִי לַגֶּפֶן וְכוּ׳ כִּבֵּס בַּיַּיִן וְכוּ׳ חַכְלִילִי עֵינַיִם מִיָּיִן וְכוּ׳, כִּי כָּל זֶה הוּא בְּחִינַת כּוֹס יַיִן שֶׁל בְּרָכָה, בְּחִינַת יַיִן דִּקְדֻשָּׁה, יַיִן הַמְשַׂמֵּחַ שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת שֶׁחֲמִימוּת הַדָּמִים נִכְלָלִין בִּקְדֻשָּׁה, לְהִתְלַהֵב לַה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל יָדָם בְּשִׂמְחָה גְּדוֹלָה, שֶׁזֶּה זוֹכִין עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת מֹשֶׁה וְדָוִד שֶׁנִּכְלָלִין יַחַד, דְּהַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת מַחֲשָׁבָה וְדִבּוּר אַזְהָרַת הַתּוֹרָה וְהַהִתְגַּבְּרוּת לְקַיֵּם הַתּוֹרָה, לֶאֱהֹב ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּשְׁנֵי יִצְרֵינוּ וְכוּ׳, שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, תּוֹרָה וּתְפִלָּה כַּנַּ״ל, שֶׁכָּל זֶה נִתְקַיֵּם עַל יְדֵי רִבּוּי הַסְּפָרִים הַקְּדוֹשִׁים שֶׁל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁמִּתְרַבִּין מְאֹד עַל יְדֵי הַדְּפוּס, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִכְלָלִין תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהַסְּפָרִים הַקְּדוֹשִׁים מְבָאֲרִים לָנוּ הֵיטֵב הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהֵם פֵּרוּשֵׁי וּבֵאוּרֵי הַתּוֹרָה לַאֲמִתּוֹ, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה עִקַּר נִצְחוֹן הַמִּלְחָמָה, שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּחִינַת יַיִן דִּקְדֻשָּׁה וְכוּ׳ כַּנַּ״ל. וְעַל כֵּן נִסְמַךְ אֹסְרִי לַגֶּפֶן וְכוּ׳ לְפָסוּק לֹא יָסוּר שֵׁבֶט וּמְחֹקֵק כַּנַּ״ל, שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז עַל תּוֹעֶלֶת הַדְּפוּס שֶׁהוּא קִיּוּם הַתּוֹרָה וְכַנַּ״ל.

וְזֶה בְּחִינַת (שיר השירים ח) ׳שִׂימֵנִי כַּחוֹתָם עַל לִבֶּךָ כַּחוֹתָם עַל זְרוֹעֶךָ כִּי עַזָּה כַמָּוֶת אַהֲבָה׳ וְכוּ׳. חוֹתָם זֶה בְּחִינַת הַדְּפוּס שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת חֲקִיקָה וְחוֹתָם, שֶׁכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מְבַקֶּשֶׁת מֵה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁתִּתְקַשֵּׁר אֵלָיו בֶּאֱמֶת עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת הַחוֹתָם שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַדְּפוּס, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְרַבִּין הַסְּפָרִים הַקְּדוֹשִׁים שֶׁהֵם קִיּוּם הַתּוֹרָה כַּנַּ״ל.

וְזֶהוּ ׳כִּי עַזָּה כַמָּוֶת אַהֲבָה וְכוּ׳ רְשָׁפֶיהָ רִשְׁפֵּי אֵשׁ וְכוּ׳, הַיְנוּ שֶׁהַגְּבוּרוֹת, שֶׁהֵם חֲמִימוּת הַדָּמִים, נִתְהַפְּכוּ אֶל הַקְּדֻשָּׁה, וּשְׂמֹאל נִכְלַל בְּיָמִין לְהִתְלַהֵב עַל יָדָם דַּיְקָא בְּשַׁלְהוּבִין דִּרְחִימוּתָא כַּנַּ״ל, שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת כְּלִילוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, מֹשֶׁה וְדָוִד, שֶׁזֶּה זוֹכִין עַל יְדֵי רִבּוּי הַסְּפָרִים הַקְּדוֹשִׁים שֶׁמִּתְרַבִּין עַל יְדֵי הַדְּפוּס שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת חוֹתָם דִּקְדֻשָּׁה כַּנַּ״ל.

קסט

(הלכות יין נסך הלכה ג׳ אות ה׳)
segments.en:
He prophesied concerning the proliferation of books and the invention of printing, through which books would multiply without end close to the coming of the Messiah; all of them are needed for the world to draw near through them to the Holy One, blessed be He.

“The scepter shall not depart from Judah, nor the lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh comes” (49:10).

This is the aspect of printing: the blessed Lord had compassion upon us at the end of days and introduced the wisdom of printing into the world so that holy books would multiply in the world. For our Rabbis of blessed memory said (Gittin 60): You are not permitted to recite written matters orally; you are not permitted to recite oral matters in writing. For it has already been explained that the Written Torah and the Oral Torah are the aspect of Moses and David, the aspect of Torah and prayer, which are the aspect of thought and speech, which are the aspect of Moses’s remembrance and admonition, and of prevailing to win the war, which is the aspect of David, as above. And each of these two aspects needs the other, and one cannot exist without the other, as above.

This is the aspect of the Written Torah and the Oral Torah: both are necessary. The Torah’s principal completeness comes precisely through both, and there is not one without the other, as it is said, “The judgments of the Lord are truth; they are righteous together,” and as Rashi explained there, see there. For the Written Torah without the Oral Torah has no completeness at all, for one knows no law or how to perform any commandment without the Oral Torah. Likewise, the Oral Torah without the Written Torah is also not completeness, for the whole essential Oral Torah rests upon the Written Torah, since the Oral Torah is the explanation of the Written Torah. For there is no matter that is not alluded to in the Torah.

The essential Written Torah is the aspect of remembrance, as it is said, “Write this as a remembrance in the book”; that is, the aforementioned aspect of Moses’s admonitions, which is the aspect of remembrance that reminds and admonishes every limb of the commandments dependent upon him, as above. Therefore it is in writing, for the principal remembrance is in writing, since orally one can forget entirely. Therefore it must specifically be written, so that remembrance will endure, which comes specifically through writing. Therefore you are not permitted to recite written matters orally, for the principal admonition and remembrance come through writing, as above. But oral matters must specifically be said orally, and it is forbidden to say them in writing. For the Oral Torah is the aspect of coming to action, as above, which is possible only through speech of the mouth; through holy speech of the mouth, the severities are transformed into lovingkindnesses, etc., which is the principal victory in the war, etc., as above. Therefore they must specifically be said orally, and it is forbidden to say them in writing, for writing is only for remembrance.

But it is difficult to come to action through writing, for it is impossible to explain in writing all the details of the commandments and their fine points and all the ways of practices and ways in serving the blessed Creator. For the evil inclination and its forces, which take hold of the turbidity of the blood, prevail greatly within every person and greatly confuse his mind, and exert themselves to overturn the truth. Therefore it is impossible to clarify everything in writing, for matters written in a book can be diverted from the truth and interpreted according to one’s will. And as has been found with many, many people who overturned the words of the living God and interpreted the Written Torah with foreign interpretations, not according to the words of our Rabbis of blessed memory, and exposed meanings in the Torah contrary to the law and came to great heresies through their foreign interpretations; for in writing it is impossible to clarify the truth to its ultimate extent, because each person can interpret the written matters according to his will.

Therefore the blessed Lord gave us all the Torah’s laws and explanations orally, for from mouth to mouth one can explain and interpret well the truth in its absolute truth: all the Torah’s laws, ways, and counsels in their truth. But orally alone, without writing, is also not completeness, because orally it has no foundation and remembrance, and over the course of many days it could, God forbid, be forgotten entirely. Therefore both are necessary, writing and oral transmission distinctly, to preserve admonition and remembrance, for written matters endure forever. Oral transmission is needed to explain the truth of the laws and the Torah’s ways well, in absolute truth, which can be explained only specifically by mouth.

But over the course of many days, when the exiles intensified and our Rabbis of blessed memory were concerned lest the Oral Torah be forgotten from Israel, God forbid, they therefore permitted writing also the Oral Torah, because “It is time to act for the Lord; they have annulled Your Torah.” For they saw that the concern about forgetting was worse than the concern inherent in writing, lest they interpret it according to their will, God forbid; for the concern about forgetting is worse. Therefore they permitted writing the Oral Torah as well. But when writing the Oral Torah one must write very, very much, to explain and interpret well the truth in its absolute truth, for the reader can interpret matters written in a book according to his will, as above. Therefore the matter must be explained and interpreted well through several interpretations and explanations, and an interpretation of the interpretations, so that one who errs cannot err away from the true interpretation and intention.

As we see, from the day they began writing the Oral Torah, very many books multiplied in the world, for it is impossible otherwise, as above. Especially since the hearts continually diminish and the minds grow weaker, as our Rabbis of blessed memory said: “And we are like a peg in a wall for learning,” etc.; see there in Eruvin. And as is explained in all the authors’ books, therefore many books are continually needed to explain well the intention of the words of our Rabbis of blessed memory.

As we see, the Rif abridged the Gemara’s rulings in his holy books. Afterwards books multiplied to explain and interpret his words, or to dispute his words where his words did not seem right to them; afterwards books were composed concerning the Rif’s commentators. Likewise with the other books, etc. All of them are greatly needed by the world, and if these books had not existed, we would now know no law at all.

Likewise, in the ways of moral instruction and fear, and counsels and ways for serving the blessed Creator, these holy books continually multiply, to explain and reveal well to us the truth of the ways and counsels for meriting truly to serve the blessed Creator. The longer the exile continues, through our many sins, and the more the hearts diminish, the more books are continually needed to explain well the truth of the intention, to break the jaws of iniquity, to disabuse those who err and the heretics, so that they cannot overturn them and divert them from the truth, God forbid.

Therefore, over the course of many days, when the blessed Lord saw that the exile was intensifying still further and the hearts were diminishing very, very greatly, and very many books were needed, the Lord therefore had compassion on His people, and in His wondrous mercies brought it about and introduced into the world the wisdom of the craft of printing, so that many books would multiply in the world. For given the multitude of books in these generations, it would have been impossible to write them in any manner; in truth we need all of them. For certainly it is now impossible for us to know the Torah’s laws thoroughly unless we have books of the Talmud, with Rashi’s commentary and additions, and Maharsha and other commentators, and the Rif’s books with all their commentaries; and the books of the Rosh and Rambam and his commentators, and the Tur and its commentators, and the books of the later authorities, the Bais Yosef and Rema and their commentators, etc., and books of questions and answers, etc. The great authorities use all these in their books of responsa when they wish to clarify a law for us in its truth. Without all the aforementioned books and more than them, it is impossible now to clarify the law in its truth. Likewise, in the ways of counsels and moral instruction in serving the Lord, all the books of the Midrashim and their interpretations are needed, and the books of the holy Zohar and the writings of the Ari of blessed memory, and Raishis Chochmah, etc., etc.

Therefore how precious are the blessed Lord’s lovingkindnesses: He had compassion upon us and gave us the craft of printing, through which books multiply easily and very cheaply. There are many books in every city and with each and every person, and through this the Torah endures in Israel now; for when writing the Oral Torah one must write very much to explain the truth in its absolute truth. In each and every generation, as the hearts diminish still further, one must explain more and increase holy books still more. As our master of blessed memory wrote (in section 61), there are already many books and still more books are destined to exist; all of them are greatly needed by the world, and it is forbidden to mock any one of them, etc. This is what is said, “And beyond these, my son, be warned: making many books has no end.” Rashi explained, “Beyond what is written, ‘be warned’ to fulfill the sages’ words orally. And if you say, why were they not written? Making many books has no end; if we undertook to write, we would not manage to do so.” That is as above: if one wishes to write oral matters, one must write very much, as above.

Therefore the craft of printing is a great kindness, for through it very many books can be printed, as above, through which the Torah will not be forgotten from Israel, as above.

Concerning this our father Jacob prophesied when he blessed Judah, from whom the Messiah came forth: “The scepter shall not depart from Judah, nor the lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh comes.” The lawgiver is printing: he prophesied that “the scepter shall not depart from Judah”—this is the aspect of the scribe’s staff, the aspect of writing the holy books of the Torah. “And the lawgiver” is the aspect of printing: the wisdom of printing would be revealed in the world, and the engraving and printing of Israel’s books would not be annulled. “Until Shiloh comes”—this is the Messiah. For through the multitude of holy books, through the wisdom of printing, the Torah will not be forgotten until Shiloh comes: this is Moses, the Messiah.

And this is “And to him shall be the gathering of peoples, binding his foal to the vine,” etc., “He washed in wine,” etc., “His eyes are red from wine,” etc. For in the future, when the Messiah comes, Moses and David will then be included together in ultimate unity, for Shiloh is Moses, who is the Messiah. Likewise David is the Messiah, as it is said, “The anointed one of the God of Jacob”; for the Messiah’s soul will be composed of both, Moses and David. Then the redemption will be complete, with no exile after it, for we will merit to remember Moses’s admonitions and fulfill them completely through the aspect of David. For both, Moses and David, will be included together. This is the aspect of “Until Shiloh comes, and to him shall be the gathering of peoples”: all the peoples, which are the seventy nations, will be transformed into holiness and will all gather to Moses, the Messiah. This is the aforementioned aspect: the blood is included in holiness, the left is included in the right, etc., as above. This is the aspect of holy wine, which is the aspect of David, as above.

And this is what is juxtaposed immediately: “Binding to the vine,” etc., “He washed in wine,” etc., “His eyes are red from wine,” etc. For all this is the aspect of a cup of wine of blessing, the aspect of holy wine, wine that gladdens, which is the aspect of the heat of the blood being included in holiness, to become aflame for the blessed Lord through it with great joy. This is merited through the aspect of Moses and David included together, namely the aspect of thought and speech, the admonition of the Torah and the exertion to fulfill the Torah, to love the blessed Lord with both our inclinations, etc. This is the aspect of the Written Torah and the Oral Torah, Torah and prayer, as above. All this is sustained through the multitude of holy books of the Torah, which multiply greatly through printing; through this, the Written Torah and the Oral Torah are included together, through the holy books explaining well to us the Oral Torah, which consists of interpretations and explanations of the Torah in its truth. Through this comes the principal victory in the war, which is the aspect of holy wine, etc., as above. Therefore “Binding to the vine,” etc., is juxtaposed to the verse “The scepter shall not depart, nor the lawgiver,” as above, which alludes to the benefit of printing, which is the preservation of the Torah, as above.

This is the aspect of (Song of Songs 8), “Set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm, for love is strong as death,” etc. A seal is the aspect of printing, which is the aspect of engraving and a seal. The congregation of Israel asks of the blessed Lord that she become bound to Him in truth through the aspect of the seal, which is the aspect of printing, through which the holy books multiply, which are the preservation of the Torah, as above.

And this is “For love is strong as death,” etc., “Its flashes are flashes of fire,” etc. That is, the severities, which are the heat of the blood, were transformed into holiness, and the left is included in the right, to become aflame precisely through them in flames of love, as above. This is the aspect of the inclusion of the Oral Torah and the Written Torah, Moses and David, which is merited through the multitude of holy books that multiply through printing, which is the aspect of a seal of holiness, as above.

pairs.he: התנבא על ריבוי הספרים והמצאת הדפוס שעל ידי זה יתרבו ספרים אין קץ סמוך לביאת משיח וכולם נצרכים לעולם להתקרב ע״י להקב״ה
pairs.en: He prophesied concerning the proliferation of books and the invention of printing, through which books would multiply without end close to the coming of the Messiah; all of them are needed for the world to draw near through them to the Holy One, blessed be He.

pairs.he: זֶה בְּחִינַת הַדְּפוּס שֶׁחָמַל עָלֵינוּ ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּאַחֲרִית הַיָּמִים וְהִמְצִיא בָּעוֹלָם חָכְמַת הַדְּפוּס כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְרַבּוּ סְפָרִים קְדוֹשִׁים בָּעוֹלָם. כִּי אָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (גיטין ס) דְּבָרִים שֶׁבִּכְתָב אִי אַתָּה רַשַּׁאי לְאָמְרָם בְּעַל פֶּה, דְּבָרִים שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה אִי אַתָּה רַשַּׁאי לְאָמְרָם בִּכְתָב. כִּי כְּבָר מְבֹאָר שֶׁתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה זֶה בְּחִינַת מֹשֶׁה, וְדָוִד בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה וּתְפִלָּה שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת מַחֲשָׁבָה וְדִבּוּר, שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת הַזִּכָּרוֹן וְהָאַזְהָרָה שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה, וְהַהִתְגַּבְּרוּת לְנַצֵּחַ הַמִּלְחָמָה, שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת דָּוִד כַּנַּ״ל. וּשְׁנֵי הַבְּחִינוֹת הָאֵלּוּ כָּל אֶחָד צָרִיךְ לַחֲבֵרוֹ וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָאֶחָד בְּלֹא חֲבֵרוֹ כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: This is the aspect of printing: the blessed Lord had compassion upon us at the end of days and introduced the wisdom of printing into the world so that holy books would multiply in the world. For our Rabbis of blessed memory said (Gittin 60): You are not permitted to recite written matters orally; you are not permitted to recite oral matters in writing. For it has already been explained that the Written Torah and the Oral Torah are the aspect of Moses and David, the aspect of Torah and prayer, which are the aspect of thought and speech, which are the aspect of Moses’s remembrance and admonition, and of prevailing to win the war, which is the aspect of David, as above. And each of these two aspects needs the other, and one cannot exist without the other, as above.

pairs.he: וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם צְרִיכִין. וְעִקַּר שְׁלֵמוּת הַתּוֹרָה עַל יְדֵי שְׁנֵיהֶם דַּיְקָא, וְאֵין אֶחָד בְּלֹא חֲבֵרוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר. ״מִשְׁפְּטֵי ה׳ אֱמֶת צָדְקוּ יַחְדָּו״, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁפֵּרֵשׁ רַשִׁ״י שָׁם, עַיֵּן שָׁם. כִּי תוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב בְּלֹא שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה אֵין לָהּ שׁוּם שְׁלֵמוּת. כִּי אֵין יוֹדְעִין שׁוּם דִּין וְאֵיךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת שׁוּם מִצְוָה בְּלֹא תוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה. וְכֵן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בְּלֹא תוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב גַּם כֵּן אֵינוֹ שְׁלֵמוּת. כִּי כָּל עִקַּר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה נִסְמָךְ עַל תוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, כִּי תוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הִיא פֵּרוּשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב. כִּי לֵיכָּא מִלְּתָא דְּלָא רְמִיזָא בְּאוֹרַיְתָא.
pairs.en: This is the aspect of the Written Torah and the Oral Torah: both are necessary. The Torah’s principal completeness comes precisely through both, and there is not one without the other, as it is said, “The judgments of the Lord are truth; they are righteous together,” and as Rashi explained there, see there. For the Written Torah without the Oral Torah has no completeness at all, for one knows no law or how to perform any commandment without the Oral Torah. Likewise, the Oral Torah without the Written Torah is also not completeness, for the whole essential Oral Torah rests upon the Written Torah, since the Oral Torah is the explanation of the Written Torah. For there is no matter that is not alluded to in the Torah.
